Zepz (formerly Sendwave and WorldRemit, merged 2021) is a London-based digital money-transfer company. Its apps, WorldRemit and Sendwave, let migrants send money from countries such as the UK, US, Canada and Europe to mobile wallets, bank accounts and cash pickup in Africa, Asia and Latin America. It earns fees and foreign-exchange margin on transfers, serving millions of retail customers across roughly 130 countries. Privately held and venture-backed, with over $1bn raised. Consumer fintech brand with solid awareness within diaspora communities, little mainstream profile.

Voi is a Stockholm-based micromobility operator running shared e-scooters and e-bikes in more than 100 cities across Europe, mainly the Nordics, UK, Germany, Italy and Spain. Consumers rent vehicles through its app, paying per minute or by pass, and cities grant operating licences. Founded in 2018, it has raised roughly $766m in equity and debt and reported profitability in recent years. It is privately held and a Swedish unicorn. Strong consumer street-level brand visibility in European cities, with a young urban user base.

JAC Motors (Anhui Jianghuai Automobile Group) is a state-owned Chinese vehicle maker based in Hefei, Anhui. It builds light, medium and heavy commercial trucks, passenger cars, buses and engines, and sells under JAC and electric brands, partnering with Volkswagen on the JAC-Volkswagen (Sehol) EV venture. Revenue comes from vehicle sales in China and exports to Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Owned by the Anhui provincial government, with a listed subsidiary on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Known mainly in emerging markets; limited Western consumer awareness.

Lizy is a Brussels-based digital vehicle leasing provider for businesses and self-employed professionals, offering online long-term car leasing in Belgium through a fully digital process, with fleet management and financing built in. It earns lease and service fees from corporate customers and individuals using company-car schemes. Backed by venture and debt funding of about EUR415m, according to Crunchbase. A private, growing fintech and mobility player. B2B and local, so brand awareness outside Belgium is low.

Niron Magnetics is a Minneapolis start-up developing permanent magnets made from iron nitride, a rare-earth-free material, to replace neodymium magnets used in electric vehicle motors, wind turbines and industrial motors. It spun out of University of Minnesota research and is building a commercial plant in Sartell, Minnesota. Customers are motor and EV makers and their suppliers, and it raised about $470m including support from the US Department of Energy and investors such as Stellantis Ventures and GM Ventures. Private, B2B deep-tech with no consumer brand profile.

Also is a Palo Alto electric micromobility company launched in 2024 as a Rivian spin-out, building lightweight electric vehicles including the TM-B electric bike with pedal and throttle modes, plus software and services. It sells to consumers and fleets, and raised a reported $200m from Rivian and investors, with total funding of about $455m per Crunchbase. Private, headquartered in California, with initial sales focused on the US. Early-stage consumer brand, still building awareness, though linked to the better-known Rivian name.

Canada Cartage is a Mississauga, Ontario transportation and logistics provider offering dedicated fleet solutions, general freight, truckload and warehousing, with a large fleet of tractors and trailers serving retail, grocery, and industrial customers across Canada and the US. It makes money from contracted transportation and supply chain services. Funding of about $400m per Crunchbase reflects its private-equity-backed ownership. B2B logistics brand, trucks carry its name on the road but it has little consumer awareness.

Dorman Products is a US supplier of aftermarket automotive replacement parts, based in Colmar, Pennsylvania. It sells tens of thousands of products, including hardware, fasteners, brake parts, engine components and fluid parts under brands such as Dorman, HELP! and Dorman OE FIX, mainly for vehicles that are out of warranty. Customers are auto parts retailers like AutoZone, Advance and O'Reilly, plus distributors, in North America and abroad. Listed on Nasdaq (DORM), annual sales over $1.9bn. Sold through retail shelves under its own brand, mostly known to mechanics and DIY drivers.

TMD Friction is a Leverkusen, Germany manufacturer of brake pads, linings and friction materials. Its brands include Textar, Don and Mintex, and it supplies original equipment to car, truck, rail and industrial makers plus the independent aftermarket. It operates plants in Europe, Asia and the Americas, employing several thousand people. Owned by Nisshinbo (Japan) after a 2019 deal replaced earlier private-equity ownership by Charterhouse. Largely B2B, though Textar and Mintex are known to garages and enthusiasts; low direct consumer awareness.

Acrisure is a Grand Rapids, Michigan financial services firm that began as an insurance broker and has grown through hundreds of acquisitions. It offers insurance brokerage, reinsurance, employee benefits, asset and wealth management, cyber services, real estate services and AI-driven insurance technology to businesses and individuals worldwide. It reports revenue of several billion dollars and tens of thousands of staff in over 100 countries. Privately held, backed by investors including Blackstone, Bain and Mubadala. Acrisure holds naming rights to Acrisure Stadium, the Pittsburgh Steelers' home, and is active in sports sponsorship.

Crusoe is a Denver-based AI infrastructure company that builds and operates data centers and a GPU cloud for AI training and inference. Starting from flared-gas-powered computing, it now develops large campuses such as the Abilene, Texas site for OpenAI and Oracle's Stargate project. Customers are AI labs and enterprises renting compute capacity. It has raised billions in equity and debt, with valuation reported above $10bn. The input lists the name as Nexus Data Centers, likely a variant. B2B infrastructure with limited consumer awareness but high profile in tech and investor circles.

Lowe's is the second-largest US home improvement retailer, headquartered in Mooresville, North Carolina. It operates about 1,700 stores in the US and Canada selling appliances, tools, building materials, hardware, lawn and garden products and home decor, to homeowners, DIY customers and professional contractors, online and in store. Annual revenue is around $80-85bn with roughly 300,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (LOW). Very high consumer brand visibility in North America and a long-time major sports sponsor, notably NASCAR, where it has been a headline sponsor of Hendrick Motorsports.

MasOrange is Spain's largest telecom operator, formed in 2024 when Orange Spain and MasMovil merged in a joint venture owned equally by Orange and a Lorca consortium (KKR, Cinven and Providence). It provides mobile, fixed broadband, fibre and TV to tens of millions of consumer and business lines under brands including Orange, Yoigo, MasMovil, Pepephone and Lowi. Annual revenue is about EUR7bn. Privately held, Madrid-based. Orange is well known to Spanish consumers and the group is a visible advertiser and sponsor in Spain.

Medtronic is one of the world's largest medical device makers, with operational headquarters in Minneapolis and legal base in Galway, Ireland. It sells cardiac devices (pacemakers, defibrillators), diabetes pumps and sensors, surgical robotics, neuromodulation, spine and vascular products to hospitals and health systems in over 150 countries. Revenue is about $32bn with roughly 95,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (MDT). Primarily B2B and clinician-facing, but a widely recognised healthcare brand; it has used sports sponsorship for awareness, including marathon and cycling links.

NEOM is a Saudi Arabian giga-project in the northwest of the country, owned by the Public Investment Fund and headed from Riyadh. It is planned as a set of new developments including The Line linear city, Oxagon industrial port, Trojena mountain resort (host of the 2029 Asian Winter Games), Sindalah island and the Magna region, with a focus on tourism, green hydrogen, real estate and technology. Funding comes from the PIF and bonds, with spending in the tens of billions of dollars. Government-backed. NEOM is a prominent sponsor, with partnerships in football, sailing, McLaren's Extreme E and other global sport.

Scale AI is a San Francisco company that provides data labeling, evaluation and data infrastructure used to train AI models. Its platform, using a managed workforce and software, serves AI labs, large tech firms and the US government, including defence contracts. Founded in 2016 by Alexandr Wang, it was valued at about $14bn after Meta bought a 49% stake for roughly $14.3bn in 2025, and Wang joined Meta. Private. B2B, well known in AI and technology circles but with little consumer awareness.

Sumisho Air Lease is an aircraft leasing company, a subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Corporation, with a US office in Los Angeles. It buys commercial aircraft and engines and leases them to airlines, earning rental income and sale gains, and was later merged into the Sumitomo group aviation leasing platform. Funding of about $19bn in the input appears to be a debt or facility figure and may be garbled by OCR. B2B lessor with no consumer profile, and a poor sponsorship target.

Affirm is a San Francisco fintech offering buy-now-pay-later loans at online and in-store checkouts. It partners with merchants such as Amazon, Shopify, Walmart and Apple, and earns merchant fees, interest on loans and interchange from its debit card. Customers are US, Canadian and UK shoppers, and the company reports annual gross merchandise volume above $30bn. Founded in 2012 by Max Levchin, it listed on the Nasdaq (AFRM) in 2021. Consumer-facing brand with strong US awareness through checkout buttons; it has run sports sponsorships including the NFL and Premier League deals.

Amazon Seller Services is the Indian entity of Amazon that operates the Amazon.in online marketplace, connecting millions of third-party sellers with Indian shoppers and providing logistics, payments and advertising services. It earns commissions, fulfilment and ad fees. Based in Bengaluru, it is a wholly owned subsidiary of Amazon.com, which has committed billions of dollars to India. The consumer brand Amazon is hugely visible in India, and the company advertises and sponsors heavily, including cricket.

Anysphere is the San Francisco AI company behind Cursor, an AI-powered code editor built on VS Code that helps developers write, edit and debug code using large language models. It sells subscriptions to individual developers and enterprises, and reported annualised revenue above $500m in 2025, growing very quickly. Founded in 2022, it has raised several billion dollars at a valuation reported near $29bn in late 2025, with backers including Thrive, a16z, Accel and Nvidia. Private. Widely known among developers, little mainstream consumer awareness.

Aspen Technology (AspenTech) is a Bedford, Massachusetts industrial software company providing process simulation, asset optimisation and AI-based software for energy, chemicals, mining and engineering firms. Customers include oil and gas, chemical and utility companies worldwide, paying licence and subscription fees. Revenue is about $1bn. Emerson Electric took a majority stake in 2022, then bought out the remainder in 2025, taking it private from the Nasdaq (AZPN). B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer awareness.

Booking Holdings is the world's largest online travel company, headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut. Its brands include Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, offering hotel and flight reservations, car rentals and restaurant bookings, earning commissions and advertising fees. Revenue is above $23bn with about 24,000 employees, serving travellers in 200+ countries. Listed on Nasdaq (BKNG). Booking.com is a major consumer brand with huge advertising spend, and the group has used sports sponsorship, including Booking.com's tie-ups in football and with Formula 1 rival series.

Claritev Corporation is the 2025 rebrand of MultiPlan, a McLean, Virginia healthcare cost management and payments technology company. It sells analytics-based claims repricing and network-access services to health insurers, self-funded employers and third-party administrators, taking fees tied to savings. It is listed on the NYSE (CTEV) and carries heavy debt following a 2021 SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp III. B2B healthcare technology provider with no consumer brand awareness.

Dream Games is an Istanbul mobile game studio, founded in 2019, best known for Royal Match, a match-3 puzzle game that is among the top-grossing mobile games worldwide. It earns from in-app purchases and advertising from tens of millions of players globally. Reported annual revenue exceeds $1bn. Backed by Index Ventures, Makers Fund and others, it raised $255m in 2021 and was valued near $2.75bn; Savvy Games Group (Saudi PIF) acquired it in 2023 for about $4.9bn. Consumer game brand with heavy advertising in many countries, which includes TV and sports.

Freepoint Commodities is a Stamford, Connecticut commodity merchant that trades and markets physical energy, metals and agricultural products, including crude oil, refined products, natural gas liquids, metals and concentrates. Customers are producers, refiners and industrial buyers worldwide, and it earns trading margins and logistics fees, with offices across Europe, Asia and the Americas. Founded in 2012. Privately held, with funding including a large investment from Hartree Partners and others. B2B trading house with little public consumer awareness.

Hudson's Bay Company was a Canadian retail group founded in 1670, and one of the oldest companies in North America. It operated Hudson's Bay department stores in Canada, and earlier owned Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord and Taylor, selling fashion, beauty and home goods. After pandemic pressures, the Canadian business sought creditor protection in March 2025 and liquidated, closing all stores by mid-2025. The Saks brands sit in separate Saks Global. Formerly a very recognisable Canadian consumer brand; now defunct as a retailer.

Level 3 Financing is a financing and holding subsidiary within the Lumen Technologies group, based in Broomfield, Colorado. It issues debt secured by Level 3 Communications' fibre network, which carries internet backbone, wavelength, Ethernet, security and cloud connectivity for enterprises, carriers and governments. The operating business is part of listed Lumen Technologies (NYSE: LUMN). Funding of about $3.9bn reflects debt raised rather than venture equity. B2B telecom infrastructure with no consumer brand profile.

MGM Resorts International is a Las Vegas hospitality and gaming company operating casino resorts including Bellagio, MGM Grand, ARIA, Cosmopolitan, Mandalay Bay and Luxor in Las Vegas, plus resorts in Macau and regional US markets, and the online sports betting and gaming business BetMGM, a joint venture with Entain. It earns from gaming, rooms, dining, entertainment and conventions, with annual revenue about $17bn. Listed on the NYSE (MGM). Very strong consumer brand and a prolific sports sponsor, with an official F1 partnership via MGM and Las Vegas Grand Prix ties.

Micron Technology is a Boise, Idaho semiconductor maker, one of the three largest producers of DRAM memory and a major NAND flash maker. It sells memory and storage chips to data centers, AI server makers, smartphone, PC, automotive and industrial customers, and sells consumer SSDs and memory under the Crucial brand. Revenue is $25bn+ with around 48,000 employees and fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan, Singapore and elsewhere. Listed on the Nasdaq (MU). Mostly a B2B brand, with Crucial giving some consumer and gamer awareness.

Nexi is a Milan-based European payments company (PayTech), formed by the merger of Nexi, Nets and SIA. It provides merchant acquiring, card issuing and processing, digital banking infrastructure and online payment services to banks, merchants and businesses across Italy, the Nordics, the DACH region and Central and Eastern Europe. It serves millions of merchants and has annual revenue around EUR3.5bn. Listed on Borsa Italiana (NEXI) with investors including Hellman and Friedman and Bain Capital. Mostly B2B, though the logo is visible at payment terminals and through sponsorships.

Nidec Corporation is a Kyoto-headquartered Japanese maker of electric motors, one of the world's largest. It produces precision small motors for hard drives, appliances and cars, plus automotive traction motors, e-axles, robotics, industrial and appliance motors and machine tools, with revenue of roughly JPY 2.3 trillion and over 100,000 staff across more than 40 countries. Customers are automakers, electronics firms and industrial companies. Listed in Tokyo (6594) and on the NYSE until delisting there. Largely B2B, well known in industry but little consumer visibility.

OneAdvanced (Advanced) is a Birmingham, UK software company that provides cloud-based business and public-sector software, covering NHS and care services, legal, education, finance, HR and payroll, and AI-enabled workflow tools. Customers are UK health, government and enterprise organisations, paying subscription fees. It has thousands of staff and annual revenue around GBP 500m+. Majority-owned by private equity firm BC Partners following a 2023 deal that valued it at about GBP 2.2bn. B2B software, with little consumer awareness.

PhonePe is a Bengaluru-based Indian digital payments and financial services platform built on the UPI system, with a leading market share of UPI transactions. Its app serves several hundred million registered users and millions of merchants, offering payments, wealth products, insurance distribution, lending referrals and merchant devices. Majority-owned by Walmart after Flipkart's 2016 acquisition and separated from Flipkart in 2022. Private, and preparing a stock market listing in India. Strong consumer brand in India with big cricket, IPL and media sponsorships.

Sandals Resorts International is a luxury all-inclusive resort operator headquartered in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and founded by Gordon Butch Stewart in 1981. It runs Sandals (couples-focused) and Beaches (family-focused) resorts across the Caribbean in Jamaica, Saint Lucia, Antigua, Barbados, Grenada, the Bahamas and elsewhere. Guests are mostly North American and UK vacationers, with revenue from room rates, packages and add-ons. Privately owned by the Stewart family, now run by Adam Stewart. Strong consumer brand recognition in the US and UK through heavy advertising.

Subway is one of the world's largest restaurant franchises, with about 37,000 locations in over 100 countries, selling made-to-order sandwiches, salads and wraps. Based in Milford, Connecticut, though Crunchbase lists a Canadian address. Operations are overwhelmingly franchised, earning royalties and fees from franchisees. In 2024 it was acquired by Roark Capital for about $9.6bn, taking over from founders' families. Private. Extremely high global consumer brand awareness and a regular sports sponsor and advertiser.

Telegram is a cloud-based messaging app founded by Pavel Durov, offering chats, large groups, channels, bots, mini apps and a crypto-linked wallet. It reports about one billion monthly active users and earns from Telegram Premium subscriptions, advertising in channels and bond and TON-related activity. Headquartered in Dubai, with a legal presence in the British Virgin Islands. Privately held by Durov, with debt financing raised through bonds. Widely known consumer app with huge usage, notably in Russia, Eastern Europe, India and the Middle East, though brand partnerships are rare.

UL Solutions is a safety science company, spun out of Underwriters Laboratories, based in Northbrook, Illinois. It provides testing, inspection, certification, auditing and software services, and the UL mark appears on billions of products such as electrical appliances and batteries. Customers are manufacturers, retailers and regulators worldwide, with revenue around $3bn and about 15,000 employees. IPO on the NYSE (ULS) in April 2024. B2B, but the UL mark is widely recognised on packaging; it has sponsored motorsport.

Unity is a San Francisco software company whose Unity engine is used to build real-time 2D and 3D games and interactive experiences, with products for game monetisation, advertising (Unity Ads, ironSource) and live-ops services. Customers are game developers, studios, automotive, film and industrial firms, paying subscriptions and revenue shares, with annual revenue about $1.8bn. Listed on the NYSE (U). B2B developer tools; widely known to game developers but little consumer brand recognition. It has been involved in motorsport marketing in the past.

Ventas is a Chicago-based real estate investment trust specialising in healthcare properties. Its portfolio of roughly 1,400 assets includes senior housing communities, medical office buildings, life science and research space, and hospitals in the US, Canada and the UK, leased to or operated by care providers. Income is rental and operating revenue, with annual revenue about $5bn and a market capitalisation in the tens of billions. Listed on the NYSE (VTR). B2B real estate owner with low consumer awareness.

Viasat is a Carlsbad, California satellite communications company supplying broadband internet through its own geostationary satellites, including ViaSat-3, to consumers, airlines, ships, enterprises and governments, plus defence and secure communications gear. In 2023 it acquired Inmarsat. Revenue is over $4bn and it employs several thousand people. Listed on Nasdaq (VSAT). Largely B2B and government, though consumer satellite internet and in-flight Wi-Fi give it some brand exposure; it has been involved in sports and technology sponsorships.

WiseTech Global is a Sydney-area logistics software company whose CargoWise platform runs freight forwarding, customs and supply chain operations for global freight forwarders, carriers and logistics providers. It has grown through many acquisitions, with annual revenue around AUD 1.3-1.4bn and thousands of staff in many countries. Founded by Richard White, it listed on the ASX (WTC) in 2016. B2B software with little consumer awareness; its customers include most of the leading freight forwarders.

Zomato (now Eternal Ltd) is a Gurugram-based Indian online food delivery and restaurant discovery platform, also operating the quick-commerce service Blinkit, going-out dining service District, and B2B supplier Hyperpure. It earns commissions, delivery and advertising fees from tens of millions of customers and hundreds of thousands of restaurants in India. It listed in Mumbai (NSE/BSE) in 2021 and renamed the group Eternal in 2025. Very strong consumer brand across India, a visible advertiser and cricket sponsor.

Another Star is based in Leiden, the Netherlands, and is described by Crunchbase as a hotel chain that operates hotels and related hospitality and leisure businesses. The input lists hospitality, hotel and leisure as its industries and shows funding of about $2.0bn, with the latest round in November 2025. The business model is likely accommodation revenue, but the input gives no further detail on brands, size or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

AWL Agri Business (formerly Adani Wilmar) is an Ahmedabad-based Indian FMCG and agri company, best known for Fortune cooking oils, plus rice, wheat flour, pulses, sugar and soaps. It sells packaged staples to Indian households and bulk oils and oleochemicals to industry, with annual revenue around INR 600bn. It was a joint venture of Adani Group and Wilmar International; Adani sold its stake to Wilmar in 2025, and the company was renamed AWL. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Fortune is a major consumer brand in India with heavy advertising.

Birkenstock Holding is a German footwear maker, headquartered in Linz am Rhein, known for contoured cork-footbed sandals such as the Arizona and Boston clog, and now a broad fashion and comfort shoe brand. It sells via wholesale, its own stores and e-commerce in over 100 countries, with revenue about EUR 2bn. Owned largely by L Catterton, the Gucci family-linked fund, after a 2021 deal, and listed on the NYSE (BIRK) since October 2023. Highly visible global consumer fashion brand, famed for the Barbie film tie-in.

Brex is a San Francisco fintech providing corporate cards, spend management, expense software, travel and banking tools for start-ups and large businesses. Customers range from early-stage tech firms to large enterprises, and it earns interchange fees, software subscriptions and interest. Founded in 2017 by Henrique Dubugras and Pedro Franceschi, it raised over $1.6bn and was valued at about $12bn in 2022. Private. B2B brand known in tech and start-up circles.

Carrefour is a French multinational retail group, based in Massy, running hypermarkets, supermarkets, convenience stores, cash-and-carry and e-commerce in France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Brazil, Argentina and other countries, with about 14,000 stores, 300,000+ staff and revenue of roughly EUR 90bn. It earns from grocery and non-food sales, plus banking, insurance and retail media. Listed on Euronext Paris (CA); the Moulin family via Galfa and Peninsula Europe are key shareholders. Very strong consumer brand, a long-time sponsor of sport such as the Tour de France and French football.

dsm-firmenich is a Dutch-Swiss company, created in 2023 by the merger of DSM and Firmenich, producing flavours, fragrances, nutritional ingredients, vitamins and health and beauty ingredients. It sells to food and drink, perfume, personal care, pharma and animal feed makers worldwide, with annual revenue around EUR 12bn and about 28,000 staff. Its animal nutrition business is being divested. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (DSFIR), with offices in Kaiseraugst and Maastricht. B2B ingredient supplier; consumers rarely see the brand, though customers include major consumer brands.

Faire is a San Francisco online wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with small and mid-sized brands, offering ordering, payment terms and shipping. Retailers in North America, Europe and beyond buy gifts, home goods, apparel and food from hundreds of thousands of brands, and Faire earns commissions and fees. Founded in 2017, it has raised over $1.7bn and was valued at about $12.4bn in 2022. Private. B2B marketplace, well known among independent shop owners but not to the general public.

Gildan is a Montreal-based manufacturer of basic apparel, selling T-shirts, fleece, socks, underwear and hosiery under brands such as Gildan, Gold Toe, Comfort Colors, American Apparel and Hanes after buying HanesBrands in a deal announced in 2025. It is vertically integrated, with plants in Central America and the Caribbean, selling mostly to screen printers and wholesale distributors, plus retailers. Revenue is around $3.3bn. Listed on the NYSE and TSX (GIL). Wholesale-focused, so the consumer brand profile is modest apart from its retail sock and underwear brands.

Hyatt Hotels Corporation is a Chicago-based global hospitality company with more than 1,400 hotels and all-inclusive resorts in about 80 countries. Brands include Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Andaz, Alila, Hyatt Place and Hyatt House, and the Hyatt Inclusive Collection. It earns fees from managed and franchised properties, plus owned hotels, with the World of Hyatt loyalty programme. Revenue is around $6.5bn. Listed on the NYSE (H), controlled by the Pritzker family trusts. Strong consumer brand, particularly among business and premium travellers.

JD Sports Fashion is a UK sports and fashion retailer based in Bury St Edmunds, operating JD, Size?, Footpatrol, Finish Line, Shoe Palace, Hibbett and Pretavous stores across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. It sells sneakers and apparel from Nike, Adidas and others, plus own-label products, through about 3,500 stores and e-commerce, with revenue near GBP 11bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (JD.). Strong youth consumer brand, active in sponsorship, including football clubs and the Premier League.

McDonald's is the world's largest restaurant chain by revenue, based in Chicago, with about 43,000 locations in over 100 countries selling burgers, fries, chicken and breakfast items. About 95 percent of restaurants are franchised, so it earns rent and royalties from franchisees plus sales at company-run units. Annual revenue is about $26bn and market capitalisation is above $200bn. Listed on the NYSE (MCD). Among the best-known consumer brands in the world and a veteran global sponsor (Olympics, FIFA World Cup, UEFA), with strong F1 relevance for family audiences.

PetSmart is the largest US pet specialty retailer, based in Phoenix, Arizona, with about 1,650 stores in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico plus e-commerce. It sells pet food, supplies and accessories, and provides grooming, training, boarding (PetsHotel), in-store Banfield veterinary clinics and adoption events. Revenue is around $10bn. Owned by private equity firm BC Partners since 2015. Private, with funding mainly debt and equity from sponsors. Strong US consumer brand with mass-market advertising.

PharmEasy is a Mumbai-based Indian online pharmacy and health platform, offering medicine delivery, diagnostic tests, teleconsultation and wholesale pharmacy supply through its owner API Holdings. It serves millions of Indian consumers and pharmacies, and has raised funds from Temasek, Prosus, TPG and others, with valuation falling sharply since a 2021 peak. In 2025 it undertook a major recapitalisation. Private. Notable consumer health brand in India, with advertising presence including cricket-linked campaigns.

Procter and Gamble is the world's largest consumer packaged goods company, based in Cincinnati, Ohio. Its brands include Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Oral-B, Pantene, Head and Shoulders, Always, Febreze, Olay and Ariel, sold through retailers in about 180 countries. Revenue is about $84bn with around 108,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (PG). Gillette and other brands are vast consumer names, and P&G is a long-standing Olympic partner and big sports advertiser.

Red Sea Global is a Saudi Arabian developer of luxury regenerative tourism destinations on the Red Sea coast, owned by the Public Investment Fund and based in Riyadh. Projects include The Red Sea (a set of islands and resorts with Six Senses, Ritz-Carlton and others, opened 2023) and Amaala, plus a private airport, utilities and the Red Sea International Airport. It earns from hotel, real estate and operating revenue and is state-backed. Government-owned. It is a growing sports-sponsorship name, with deals in football and sailing.

US Foods is a Rosemont, Illinois foodservice distributor, supplying restaurants, hospitals, schools, hotels and other customers with food and supplies from about 70 distribution centres. It sells fresh and frozen products, plus private-label lines such as Chef's Store cash-and-carry, with revenue around $38bn and about 30,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (USFD). B2B, with little consumer awareness, though its trucks are widely seen in the US; it has used sports sponsorship such as stadium partnerships.

Zepto is a Mumbai-based Indian quick-commerce company founded in 2021, delivering groceries and household goods to customers in about 10 minutes from dark stores in major cities. Its app serves millions of urban consumers and earns from product margins, delivery and advertising, with funding of about $2.5bn including raises led by Motilal Oswal and Nexus, valuing it near $7bn in 2025. Private. Strong urban consumer brand in India, with heavy marketing including IPL cricket advertising.

Electrolux is a Stockholm-based Swedish appliance maker, selling refrigerators, ovens, washing machines, dishwashers, vacuum cleaners and air purifiers under Electrolux, AEG, Frigidaire and Westinghouse brands to consumers across Europe, North and Latin America, Asia and Australia. Revenue is about SEK 130bn and it employs around 45,000 people, with manufacturing in many countries. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ELUX B). Large household-name brand with strong visibility in Europe, and active in sports and F1-adjacent sponsorships in some markets.

Alpaca is a San Mateo, California brokerage infrastructure company providing APIs for stock, options and crypto trading, used by fintech apps, banks and developers. Its customers include brokers and apps in the US and Asia, and it earns from payments for order flow, interest and fees. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $763m in total, including a Series D in 2026. Private. Mainly B2B and developer-focused, little consumer awareness.

Command Alkon is a Hilliard, Ohio software company serving the heavy building materials industry, supplying dispatch, ticketing, ordering and logistics software for ready-mixed concrete, aggregates and asphalt producers worldwide. Its customers are material producers and contractors, paid through software subscriptions and licences. Majority-owned by private equity firm Thoma Bravo, which acquired it in 2021 (originally from Francisco Partners). Private. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

Digital Asset is a New York blockchain software company that created the Daml smart contract language and the Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain used by banks and financial institutions for tokenisation, settlement and collateral. Customers include banks, asset managers and market infrastructure firms. Its investors include Goldman Sachs, DTCC, Citadel Securities, BNP Paribas and Circle. Private, having raised about $857m. B2B fintech with little public brand awareness.

Kitopi is a Dubai-based cloud kitchen company that operates delivery-only kitchens and partners with restaurant brands to prepare food centrally for delivery apps in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the US. It makes money from food-preparation fees and a share of orders. Founded in 2018, it was valued above $1bn in 2022 and has raised about $850m, with backers including Prosus and Cathay Innovation, and restructured after cutting costs. Private. Low consumer visibility, mostly in the restaurant trade and delivery sector.

Mews is an Amsterdam-headquartered cloud hospitality platform, providing property management, payments, booking engine and guest-experience software for hotels, hostels and resorts. Customers are thousands of hotels in 85+ countries, paying subscriptions and payment fees. Founded in 2012 in Prague, it has raised over $800m, including a $110m round in 2025 that valued it above $1.2bn, and acquired Rialto and others. Private. B2B software, known within hotels, not to guests.

Optasia is a Dubai-headquartered fintech that offers airtime and data credit, mobile money loans and other financial services through mobile operators and wallet providers in Africa, Asia and the Middle East. It works with telecoms such as MTN, Airtel and Vodacom and serves tens of millions of end users, earning fees from each credit advance. Listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (OPA) in November 2025. Backed earlier by Ardian and other investors. Mostly B2B2C, with low direct brand awareness among end users.

Playlist is described by Crunchbase as the parent company operating various physical and digital consumer businesses, headquartered in San Luis Obispo, California. The input lists apps and artificial intelligence among its industries, and shows total funding of about $785m with the latest round in January 2026. The input gives no detail on specific brands, customers, size or ownership, so the exact business model is unclear. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Propel Holdings is a Toronto fintech that provides online consumer loans and credit products to underserved borrowers in the US, Canada and the UK through brands such as MoneyKey, CreditFresh, Fora Credit and Kikoff, plus credit-as-a-service partner programmes. It earns interest and fees using AI-driven underwriting. Founded in 2012 and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (PRL) in 2023. Total funding including debt is about $800m. Consumer lending brands with limited mainstream awareness.

Ripple is a San Francisco company that provides blockchain-based cross-border payment and stablecoin technology, including RippleNet, Ripple Payments, custody services and the RLUSD stablecoin, plus the XRP Ledger and the XRP token. Customers are banks, payment providers and enterprises in many countries. Founded in 2012, it was valued at about $40bn in a 2025 share sale and has acquired Hidden Road, GTreasury and Rail. Private. Well known in crypto, and it has used sports sponsorship, including a recent US-based stadium and F1-linked marketing.

Stats Perform is a Chicago-based sports data, AI and content company supplying live and historical statistics, video, odds and predictive analytics to leagues, broadcasters, teams and betting operators. It was formed in 2019 when STATS merged with Perform Group, owner of the Opta brand. Customers are media groups, clubs, governing bodies and sportsbooks worldwide, and it earns subscription and data licensing fees. Owned by Vista Equity Partners. Private. Opta data is widely seen on TV graphics, though the company brand is B2B.

Stream is a London-based financial wellbeing platform, founded in 2018 and now in the UK, US and elsewhere, allowing employees to access earned wages early and save, borrow and manage bills through employer partnerships. Customers are employers, who offer it as a benefit to workers, and employees pay small fees. Backed by investors including Optimum and Frontline, with funding of around $767m including debt facilities. Private. Employee-benefit brand, visible to workers at partner employers but not to the wider public.

Suno is a Cambridge, Massachusetts AI music generation company whose platform lets users create full songs with vocals from text prompts. It serves consumers and creators with free and subscription plans, and has tens of millions of users. It raised $250m in November 2025 at a $2.45bn valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and Nvidia's NVentures, and reached a licensing and settlement deal with Warner Music Group. Private. High consumer awareness among online music creators, though also the subject of legal disputes with record labels.

Surf Air Mobility is a Los Angeles regional air mobility company, owning Surf Air membership flights, commuter airline Southern Airways Express and the electric aircraft powertrain developer Surf Air Mobility electrification unit. It offers subscription and per-flight travel between regional airports, mostly in the US, using Cessna Caravan aircraft. Listed on the NYSE (SRFM) since 2023, after raising about $825m. Niche consumer brand with moderate profile among frequent regional flyers and a premium customer base.

Anchorage Digital is a San Francisco-based regulated crypto custodian and infrastructure firm, holding the first national trust bank charter for digital assets from the US OCC. It provides custody, staking, settlement, trading and tokenisation services to institutions such as crypto funds, banks and corporates. Founded in 2017 and backed by Visa, Andreessen Horowitz, GIC, KKR and others, it was valued at around $3bn after a 2021 round. Private. B2B with limited public awareness, though active in crypto circles.

CDN77 is a content delivery network provider, headquartered in London with operations in Prague, serving video streaming, software downloads and websites through a global network of data centers. Customers include broadcasters, gaming firms, software companies and enterprises, charged by traffic volume and plan. It is owned by Datacamp, the Czech-based infrastructure group, which also runs BunnyCDN competitors and VPN services. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Duetti is a New York music financing and royalty platform that buys music rights and catalogues from artists, labels and rights holders, giving them upfront capital, while investors earn income from royalties. It has acquired catalog interests and offers loans and advances to artists and songwriters, backed by investment firms and about $640m in funding including debt. Private. Mostly known within the music business and fintech circles rather than to general consumers.

Gemini is a New York-based regulated cryptocurrency exchange and custodian, founded in 2014 by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss. It lets retail and institutional customers buy, sell, stake and store digital assets, and offers a crypto rewards credit card in the US. It listed on the Nasdaq (GEMI) in September 2025. Consumer-facing crypto brand with solid US awareness and a record of sports and entertainment marketing.

Hyperliquid Strategies is a New York-based digital asset treasury company formed in 2025 to hold the HYPE token of the Hyperliquid decentralised exchange, financed through a roughly $583m private placement and a merger with Sonnet BioTherapeutics, listed on Nasdaq (PURR). Its income depends on the HYPE token's price and any staking returns, and its investors include Paradigm and others. Public vehicle with no products for consumers. Low consumer awareness, but known in crypto investing.

indie Semiconductor is an Aliso Viejo, California fabless chip company focused on automotive electronics, selling chips and modules for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), LiDAR, radar, in-cabin sensing, connectivity and electrification. Customers are automakers and Tier-1 suppliers such as Aptiv, Bosch and Continental. It listed on the Nasdaq (INDI) via a 2021 SPAC merger and has acquired companies including Symeo and GEO Semiconductor. B2B component supplier, with no consumer profile.

Innoviz Technologies is an Israeli automotive LiDAR maker, with US operations noted in Santa Clara, California, whose InnovizOne and InnovizTwo sensors and perception software help vehicles see the road for autonomous driving and ADAS. Customers include automakers like BMW, Volkswagen group firm CARIAD, Mobileye (a distribution partner) and Mobileye-linked partners. Listed on Nasdaq (INVZ) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Collective Growth. B2B automotive technology supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Payoneer is a New York fintech offering cross-border payment accounts, mass payouts, working capital and card services mainly to small and medium-sized businesses, freelancers and marketplace sellers in emerging markets. It serves around 2 million customers in 190 countries and earns from transaction fees, FX spreads and interest on balances, with revenue near $1bn. It went public via SPAC on Nasdaq (PAYO) in 2021. Mostly B2B/prosumer, known to online sellers and freelancers but not widely to consumers.

SemiDrive is a Nanjing-based Chinese fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2018, specialising in automotive chips for smart cockpits, ADAS, central computing and vehicle control, covering the X9, V9, G9 and E3 families. Customers include Chinese automakers and Tier-1 suppliers, and it has shipped millions of chips with funding of around $650m from investors such as Hillhouse and Qualcomm Ventures. Private, with a Hong Kong IPO expected. B2B, without consumer brand awareness.

U GRO Capital is a Mumbai-based Indian non-bank financial company that lends to small and medium businesses, with a data-driven underwriting platform and co-lending partnerships with banks. Products include secured and unsecured working-capital and machinery loans, and it operates across India with a large branch network. Listed on the NSE and BSE (UGROCAP), with investors such as Samena Capital and Bain Capital-linked funds. B2B lender with low national consumer awareness.

AerCap is the world's largest aircraft lessor, headquartered in Dublin, with owned and managed assets of aircraft, engines and helicopters worth tens of billions of dollars. It leases planes to about 300 airlines worldwide, earning rental income and sale gains, and completed its purchase of GE Capital Aviation Services in 2021. Listed on the NYSE (AER) and led by Aengus Kelly. B2B financier, known in aviation, with no consumer awareness.

Apple is a Cupertino, California technology company that designs iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, Apple TV and Vision Pro, runs the App Store, and sells services such as iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV+, Apple Pay and AppleCare. It sells to consumers and businesses worldwide through its own stores, online and carriers, with annual revenue near $400bn and about 160,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (AAPL) and among the world's most valuable companies. Among the most recognised consumer brands; F1 US broadcast rights from 2026, and a major marketing partner.

Fab 34 JV is Intel's semiconductor manufacturing joint venture in Leixlip, County Kildare, Ireland, where Intel 4 and Intel 3 process chips are made in a large fab. In 2024 Apollo Global Management agreed to buy a 49% stake in the venture for about $11bn, funding Intel's expansion. The business is a fabrication facility with no consumer brand of its own. B2B chip production, no consumer awareness, and poor sponsorship fit.

FIS (Fidelity National Information Services) is a Jacksonville, Florida fintech that provides banking and payments technology, including core banking systems, card processing, merchant acquiring and capital markets software for banks, credit unions, corporates and merchants worldwide. It employs about 50,000 people and generates revenue near $10bn. Listed on the NYSE (FIS). It bought Global Payments' issuer business in 2025 and sold much of Worldpay. B2B, widely known in financial circles though not to consumers.

Auxmoney is a Dusseldorf-based German online lending marketplace for consumer loans, matching borrowers with private and institutional investors using credit scoring. Customers apply online for personal loans, and investors fund them, with Auxmoney earning fees. It has arranged billions of euros in loans since its 2007 founding and has been backed by investors including Santander Consumer Bank-linked partners and Bain Capital-related funds. Private. German consumer-facing fintech with moderate local awareness.

Capital One is a McLean, Virginia bank holding company and one of the largest US credit card issuers, also offering auto loans, consumer and commercial banking, savings and the Discover network after buying Discover Financial in 2025. It serves over 100 million customers and has revenue above $50bn. Listed on the NYSE (COF). The brand is very familiar to US consumers from advertising, and it is a major sports sponsor, notably holding naming rights for the Capital One Arena, the Mastercard-linked Capital One Cup and Capital One Bowl.

Concord Music Group is a Nashville-based music company covering recorded music, music publishing, theatricals and live production, with a catalogue spanning jazz, classic rock, Broadway and pop. Its labels include Fantasy, Stax, Concord Records and Rounder, and Concord Theatricals holds the rights to shows such as Rodgers and Hammerstein works. It earns royalties from streaming, licensing and live shows. Owned by Genstar Capital, GIC and Concord management, among others. Private. Brand known to the music industry; low consumer awareness.

DAZN is a London-based global sports streaming service, offering live and on-demand football, boxing, MMA, NFL, tennis and other sports to subscribers in over 200 markets, plus the Eleven and Foxtel acquisitions. It earns subscription fees and advertising, with annual revenue about GBP 3bn and tens of millions of viewers. Owned by Access Industries, led by Len Blavatnik. Private. A major consumer sports brand holding rights such as the FIFA Club World Cup 2025, and a sponsor of sports properties.

Dick's Sporting Goods is a Coraopolis, Pennsylvania (Pittsburgh area) US sporting goods retailer with about 850 Dick's stores, Golf Galaxy, Public Lands and House of Sport locations, selling equipment, apparel and footwear online and in store. It bought Foot Locker in 2025 for around $2.4bn. Annual revenue is over $13bn. Listed on the NYSE (DKS), and chaired by Edward Stack. Strong US consumer brand, with sponsorship and partnership activity across leagues, college and youth sports.

Flutter Entertainment is the world's largest online sports betting and gaming operator, with a UK registered office in Leeds and primary listing moved to the NYSE (FLUT). Brands include FanDuel, Paddy Power, Sky Bet, Betfair, PokerStars, Sportsbet and Junglee, serving tens of millions of customers in the US, UK, Ireland, Australia, Italy and India. Revenue is around $17bn. High consumer awareness and a heavy sports marketer, including league partnerships; F1 sponsor profile in betting is constrained by regulation in some markets.

Haleon is a London-based consumer health company, spun out from GSK in 2022, selling over-the-counter and everyday health products such as Sensodyne, Advil, Panadol, Voltaren, Centrum, Nicorette, Otrivin and Parodontax. It sells through pharmacies and supermarkets in more than 100 markets, with revenue about GBP 11bn and around 25,000 staff. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (HLN) and NYSE, with Pfizer having sold its stake. Many household consumer brands, and Haleon uses sports sponsorship such as Sensodyne in football and cricket.

LATAM Airlines Group is Latin America's largest airline group, headquartered in Santiago, Chile, with affiliates in Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador and Argentina, flying to over 140 destinations plus a cargo arm. It carries over 70 million passengers a year, with annual revenue near $13bn, and emerged from US Chapter 11 in 2022. Listed on the Santiago stock exchange (LTM) and NYSE ADRs. Strong regional consumer brand with sponsorship in sports across Latin America and international football.

MediaTek is a Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company based in Hsinchu, designing system-on-chips for smartphones (Dimensity), tablets, smart TVs, Wi-Fi routers, IoT devices, Chromebooks and cars. It sells to phone and electronics makers including Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo and Samsung, and is the largest smartphone chip supplier by volume. Annual revenue is about NT$ 530bn, with over 20,000 employees. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2454). Mostly B2B, though its logo appears on devices and it has sponsored sport and F1-adjacent campaigns.

Oportun is a San Mateo, California digital banking and lending company providing personal loans, credit cards, auto loans and savings to mainly Hispanic and low-to-moderate-income consumers in the US using AI-driven underwriting. It has served millions of customers and earns interest and fees. Listed on Nasdaq (OPRT). Consumer financial brand with moderate regional awareness, not yet a nationwide name.

Seagate Technology is a data storage company, legally based in Ireland and operating from Fremont, California, making hard disk drives, SSDs and storage systems for data centers, cloud providers, PCs and consumers. Its Exos drives power cloud storage, and it also sells external drives under Seagate, FireCuda and LaCie, plus Lyve services. Revenue is about $8-9bn. Listed on the Nasdaq (STX). Known by consumers through retail storage products, and a past sponsor of motorsport, including a long relationship with Williams F1 Team.

Wayflyer is a Dublin-based revenue-based financing and growth platform for e-commerce brands, providing funding for inventory and marketing along with analytics. Customers are online merchants across the US, UK, Europe, Canada and Australia, and Wayflyer earns fees on advances. Founded in 2019, it raised a $150m Series B in 2022 and debt facilities, valued at about $1.6bn, with total funding near $3.7bn including debt. Private. B2B fintech with little consumer awareness.

WM Motor was a Shanghai-based Chinese electric vehicle maker, founded 2015, selling the EX5 SUV and W6 under the Weltmeister brand. Backed by Baidu, Tencent and others, it raised billions but ran into financial trouble and filed for bankruptcy reorganisation in 2023, ending car production. A Shanghai restructuring then involved investors acquiring the assets. Funding was about $5.3bn with the last round in 2021. A defunct consumer EV brand, with no active sponsorship potential.

AGNC Investment Corp is a Bethesda, Maryland, internally managed mortgage real estate investment trust that invests mainly in agency residential mortgage-backed securities guaranteed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae. It borrows short-term via repurchase agreements and earns the spread between asset yields and funding costs, paying monthly dividends to shareholders. The portfolio is worth tens of billions of dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (AGNC), founded 2008. Funding shown reflects capital raises. Financial investment vehicle with no consumer brand profile.

AlphaSense is a New York market intelligence platform using AI to search and summarise company filings, earnings call transcripts, broker research, news and expert call transcripts. Customers are investment banks, hedge funds, asset managers and large corporations, paying subscriptions, with thousands of enterprise clients and revenue reported above $500m. It acquired Tegus in 2024. Private, valued around $4bn after a 2024 round, backed by Goldman Sachs, Viking and others. B2B, known to finance professionals, not consumers.

Altavair is described by Crunchbase as an asset management firm focused on finance and financial services, headquartered in Issaquah, Washington. The input lists finance and financial services as its industries and shows funding of about $2.4bn with the latest round in June 2026. The exact asset classes, clients and ownership are not given in the input. Likely a specialised asset or lease finance business, but unconfirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Amkor Technology is one of the largest outsourced semiconductor packaging and test providers, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. It assembles and tests chips for fabless firms and chipmakers such as Apple, Qualcomm and Nvidia, with plants in South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, China, Vietnam, Malaysia and Portugal, plus an Arizona advanced packaging site under construction. Revenue is about $6-7bn. Listed on Nasdaq (AMKR), with the founding Kim family a major shareholder. B2B manufacturing, no consumer brand awareness.

Amprion is a German electricity transmission system operator based in Dortmund, running the extra-high-voltage grid across western and southwestern Germany, around 11,000 km of lines serving roughly 29 million people. It earns regulated grid fees and is building major HVDC corridors such as A-Nord and Ultranet. Owned by a consortium of German financial investors and Mercator-linked institutions, with RWE holding a minority stake. Private. Infrastructure utility with very low consumer visibility.

ams OSRAM is an Austrian-German photonics and sensor company formed when ams AG acquired OSRAM in 2020, based in Premstaetten, Austria with Munich operations. It makes LEDs, lasers, optical sensors and microsensors used in smartphones, cars (headlights, interior lighting), industrial and medical devices. Customers include automakers, Apple and other electronics firms. Revenue is about EUR 3.4bn with roughly 20,000 employees. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (AMS). B2B component maker, though the Osram name is known to consumers from lighting.

Applied Optoelectronics is a Sugar Land, Texas maker of optical communications chips, lasers and transceivers for data centers, cable TV broadband, telecom and FTTH networks. Customers include hyperscale cloud operators such as Amazon and Microsoft, and cable companies, with manufacturing in Texas, Taiwan and China. Listed on Nasdaq (AAOI), founded in 1997. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars a year. B2B components supplier, no consumer awareness.

Asus Global is the Singapore-based regional subsidiary of ASUSTeK Computer, the Taiwanese maker of laptops, desktops, motherboards, graphics cards, monitors, phones and gaming brand Republic of Gamers (ROG). Asus sells through retailers and online worldwide, with group revenue above $15bn. The parent is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2357). The input shows funding of about $2bn, likely an internal or financing figure. Very strong consumer and gamer brand, and ASUS has sponsored motorsport and esports in several markets.

Autodesk is a San Francisco software company (legal base in San Francisco, with the Autodesk operations in the Bay Area) selling design and engineering tools such as AutoCAD, Revit, Maya, 3ds Max, Fusion and Autodesk Construction Cloud. Customers are architects, engineers, builders, manufacturers and media creators, paying mainly subscriptions, with revenue near $7bn. Listed on Nasdaq (ADSK). Well known to professionals, including film VFX and automotive design teams, and it has partnered with F1 teams on design technology; not a household consumer brand.

Avalon Labs is described by Crunchbase as a DeFi platform that integrates Bitcoin and other assets into decentralised lending and finance products. The input lists blockchain and cryptocurrency as its industries, shows no HQ country and a placeholder location, and reports funding of about $2.0bn with the latest round in May 2025, a figure that may be inaccurate. Customers and revenue model are not described. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Axiom Solutions International is listed by Crunchbase as an Austin, Texas company developing digital and electrical products and services, with industries including cloud computing and cloud infrastructure. The input shows funding of about $2.0bn with the latest round in October 2026. The input gives no further detail on its products, customers or ownership, and the name is generic, so identification is uncertain. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Bibby Financial Services is a UK-based provider of invoice finance, factoring, asset finance and trade finance to small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Banbury, Oxfordshire, and operating in the UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, the US and Asia. It advances funds against unpaid invoices and earns fees and interest. It is wholly owned by the Bibby Line Group, a family-controlled Liverpool shipping and financial group. Private. B2B lender, known to SMEs, with little consumer profile.

Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, with a legal presence rooted in the Cayman Islands and operations spread globally. It offers spot and derivatives trading, staking, a launchpad, payments, wallets and the BNB Chain ecosystem to well over 250 million registered users. In 2023 it pleaded guilty to US anti-money-laundering charges and paid $4.3bn. Private. Highly known crypto brand; it has used sports sponsorships (such as with Argentina's football team) but faces regulatory sensitivity in many jurisdictions.

Bitdeer Technologies is a Singapore-based Bitcoin mining company and cloud-hash provider, operating large mining data centers in Norway, Bhutan, the US, Ethiopia and elsewhere, and developing its own SEALMINER ASIC miners and AI cloud capacity. Backed by Jihan Wu, co-founder of Bitmain, it earns from mining rewards, hash-rate sales and hosting. Listed on Nasdaq (BTDR) since 2023 via a SPAC merger. Mainly B2B and investor-oriented, with limited consumer brand awareness.

Broadstone Net Lease is a Victor, New York, internally managed REIT that owns single-tenant commercial properties leased on a net basis, covering industrial, healthcare, restaurant, retail and office buildings across the US and Canada, with hundreds of tenants. Income is rental payments, and it pays dividends to shareholders. Listed on the NYSE (BNL) since 2020. Property investor, with no consumer brand profile.

Burford Capital is a litigation finance company, a Guernsey-registered firm with major offices in New York and London, that funds commercial legal claims and arbitrations in exchange for a share of the proceeds. It also manages funds and buys legal assets, notably its large YPF-related Argentine claim. Customers are law firms and corporate claimants. Listed on the NYSE and London markets (BUR), with a portfolio valued in the billions. B2B specialist finance firm, no consumer awareness.

Canva is an Australian online design platform, headquartered in Sydney (Surry Hills), whose templates, AI tools and drag-and-drop editor let users make presentations, social posts, videos, documents and print designs. It has over 240 million monthly active users in about 190 countries and an annual revenue above $3bn, earned from Pro, Teams and Enterprise subscriptions. Valued at around $42bn in 2025 secondary share sales. Private, founded 2013 by Melanie Perkins. Very recognisable consumer-and-business brand, with sports and F1 partnership activity including a Mercedes-AMG Petronas tie-up.

CCC Intelligent Solutions is a Chicago cloud platform for the insurance economy, supplying AI-based software for auto claims estimating, repair workflows, parts and total-loss valuation to insurers, repair shops, carmakers and parts suppliers. It links thousands of businesses in the US. Revenue is over $1bn. Listed on the NYSE (CCCS) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Dragoneer Growth Opportunities. B2B, well known to the claims industry, with no consumer brand awareness.

Cyera is a New York AI-native data security platform that discovers, classifies and protects sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises systems, with data security posture management and access controls. Customers are large enterprises, including Fortune 500 firms. Founded in Israel in 2021, it has raised over $1.7bn including a 2026 round and was valued at about $9bn. Private. B2B cybersecurity brand, known to security teams, with no consumer visibility.

East Money Information is a Shanghai-based Chinese internet financial services company running the Eastmoney.com portal and Tiantian Fund distribution platform, offering financial news, stock data, fund sales, online brokerage through East Money Securities, and wealth products. It serves many millions of retail investors in China. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (300059). A prominent consumer finance brand in China, with little presence abroad.

Embracer Group is a Swedish video game holding company, based in Karlstad, built through acquisitions. Its studios and franchises have included Tomb Raider, Metro, Dead Island, Kingdom Come, Saints Row and Borderlands publishing links, with revenue around SEK 40bn from game sales. It has been breaking itself into separately listed units, including Coffee Stain Group and Fellowship Entertainment. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (EMBRAC B). Consumer game portfolio, but the corporate brand is little known to players.

Emerson is a St. Louis, Missouri automation technology company supplying control systems, valves, measurement instruments, test and measurement tools (NI) and industrial software to process, hybrid and discrete manufacturers. Customers include oil and gas, chemical, power, life science and semiconductor firms in over 150 countries, with revenue near $17-18bn. Listed on the NYSE (EMR), and took full ownership of AspenTech in 2025. Mostly B2B, a long-standing engineering brand with little consumer visibility.

Emirates Islamic is a Dubai-based Sharia-compliant retail and corporate bank, a subsidiary of Emirates NBD, offering Islamic current and savings accounts, home and auto finance, credit cards, sukuk and business banking in the UAE. It has tens of billions of dirhams in assets and a branch network across the emirates. Owned by Emirates NBD, which is majority-owned by Investment Corporation of Dubai. Well known to UAE consumers, with sports and community sponsorship activity.

Eurofiber is a Dutch digital infrastructure company based in Maarssen, owning and operating fibre networks in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and France. It sells dark fibre, connectivity, data center interconnect, cloud and managed network services to enterprises, telecoms, government and healthcare customers. Owned by infrastructure funds including Antin and Dutch pension capital after a 2023 funding. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

ExodusPoint Capital Management is a New York multi-strategy hedge fund founded in 2018 by Michael Gelband, formerly of Millennium, investing across macro, equities, credit and systematic strategies on behalf of institutional investors with tens of billions of dollars under management. It earns management and performance fees. Offices in New York, London, Hong Kong, Singapore and elsewhere. Private. Known within institutional finance, no consumer profile.

Figure AI is a San Jose, California AI robotics company building general-purpose humanoid robots, including Figure 02 and Figure 03, together with its Helix vision-language-action model, for use in factories, logistics and eventually homes. It has run pilots with BMW and raised about $1.85bn, valued around $39bn in a 2025 round, with backers including Microsoft, Nvidia, Jeff Bezos, OpenAI and Intel. Private. High profile in technology media; not yet a mainstream consumer brand.

Fireworks AI is a San Mateo, California inference platform that serves open-source and custom AI models quickly and cheaply to developers and enterprises through APIs, fine-tuning and compute services. It was founded in 2022 by former Meta PyTorch engineers, and customers include Uber, Notion, Cursor and Samsung. Funding is about $250m raised at a valuation near $4bn in 2025. Private. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness.

Flexential is a Centennial, Colorado data center and cloud services provider, operating colocation, managed hosting, cloud, connectivity and disaster recovery services from about 40 data centers across the US. Customers are mid-size and large enterprises and technology firms. It has been owned by GI Partners and Social Capital-style investors, with Churchill Capital-backed ownership since 2021, and is private. B2B infrastructure, no consumer profile.

Fortive is a Everett, Washington industrial technology company, spun out of Danaher in 2016, whose operating units include Fluke (test equipment), Tektronix, Gordian, Accruent and Provation, Ralliant spun off in 2025. Customers are engineers, contractors, utilities and healthcare firms worldwide, with revenue near $4bn. Listed on the NYSE (FTV). Largely B2B, though Fluke is well known to technicians; no consumer brand beyond that.

Forward Industries is a design, sourcing and manufacturing company for carry cases and protective solutions, historically for medical devices (diabetic kits), tools and consumer electronics, under its Forward Industries Design Group. In 2025 it pivoted to a Solana digital asset treasury strategy, with a large private placement led by Galaxy Digital, Jump Crypto and Multicoin. Listed on Nasdaq (FORD), with the HQ shown as Austin, Texas. Small B2B supplier turned crypto treasury vehicle, with no consumer awareness.

GAC Aion New Energy Automobile is the dedicated electric vehicle brand and company of GAC Group (Guangzhou Automobile Group), based in Guangzhou. It sells the Aion S, Aion Y, Aion V and Hyper premium EV models in China and exports to Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Latin America. A 2022 round raised CNY 18.3bn from investors including Tencent and Guangzhou-linked funds. Subsidiary of state-owned GAC. Strong domestic consumer awareness in China, with growing presence abroad.

GoTo Group is an Indonesian technology group formed by the 2021 merger of Gojek and Tokopedia, based in Jakarta. It runs ride-hailing, food delivery, e-commerce, logistics and financial services (GoPay) in Indonesia and Southeast Asia, earning commissions, advertising and payment fees. It serves tens of millions of consumers and millions of driver partners and merchants. Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (GOTO), with Grab merger talks reported. Huge consumer brand in Indonesia, with sports and event sponsorships.

IGM Financial is a Winnipeg-based Canadian wealth and asset management company, part of the Power Corporation group, with Investors Group (IG Wealth Management), Mackenzie Investments and Rockefeller Capital Management stakes. It manages about C$300bn of assets for retail investors and advisors and earns fees. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (IGM). Strong Canadian consumer finance brand through advisor networks, and active in sponsorship such as Canadian sport.

Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) is a New Delhi state-owned financing arm of Indian Railways, raising funds on domestic and international bond markets to finance the purchase of rolling stock and railway projects, leasing assets to Indian Railways. It earns lease income and has a loan book around INR 4 trillion. Majority-owned by the Government of India and listed on the NSE and BSE since 2021. Government-linked funding vehicle, no consumer brand marketing.

Isomorphic Labs is a London AI drug discovery company, a sister company of Google DeepMind, founded in 2021 by Demis Hassabis to apply AlphaFold-style models to design new medicines. It has research partnerships with Eli Lilly and Novartis and raised about $600m in 2025 from Thrive Capital, with subsequent funding, owned by Alphabet. Private. Well known in science and tech circles, with no consumer products.

ITC Holdings is a Novi, Michigan electricity transmission company, the largest independent transmission operator in the US, with around 17,000 circuit miles of high-voltage lines across Michigan, Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois, Missouri, Kansas and Oklahoma. It earns regulated returns on grid investment. Owned by Fortis Inc. of Canada since 2016, with minority stakes sold to investors such as GIC and CPP Investments. B2B regulated utility with no consumer brand profile.

iwoca is a London online lender providing flexible short-term credit and loans to small businesses in the UK and Germany, using automated underwriting that links to accounting and bank data. It has lent several billion pounds to tens of thousands of SMEs since 2012, and is backed by Augmentum, Santander and Lloyds-linked funds, with debt facilities from Citi and others. Private. Known to small businesses and brokers, with a modest sponsorship record.

Joulent is listed by Crunchbase as a Houston, Texas company developing large-scale energy systems, and the input places it in artificial intelligence-related industries. Funding shown is about $1.75bn with the latest round in July 2026. The input does not say what products, customers or owners it has, and the name matches no company I can confidently identify. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Kennedy Wilson is a Beverly Hills, California global real estate investment company that owns, operates and invests in multifamily, office, industrial and hospitality property and loans, mainly in the western US, UK and Ireland. It also manages assets for institutional partners and earns rent, fees and sale gains, with around $20bn of assets under management. Listed on the NYSE (KW), led by William McMorrow. B2B property group with little consumer profile.

Macerich is a Santa Monica, California REIT that owns and manages regional shopping centres in major US markets such as Tysons Corner, Scottsdale Fashion Square, Santa Monica Place and Broadway Plaza, leasing space to retailers. Its income is rent and tenant recoveries, and its portfolio holds around 40 malls. Listed on the NYSE (MAC). Property owner, little consumer brand beyond the mall names.

Metaplanet is a Tokyo-listed company that has adopted a Bitcoin treasury strategy, holding tens of thousands of BTC on its balance sheet, and also runs a hospitality business and a Bitcoin income business. Often called Japan's MicroStrategy, it funds purchases through equity raises, preferred shares and bonds, and is quoted on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (3350). Led by Simon Gerovich. Retail-investor brand, high online profile in crypto, but no mainstream consumer products.

Motive is a San Francisco fleet management and driver safety platform, formerly KeepTruckin, offering AI dashcams, electronic logging devices, vehicle telematics, spend management and compliance tools. It serves tens of thousands of fleets in trucking, construction, oil and gas and field services across North America. Valued at $2.85bn in 2022 and raised around $2bn in total. It filed for a US IPO in 2025. B2B brand, widely seen on truck windshields but not a consumer name.

Neoen is a Paris-based French renewable energy producer developing, financing, building and operating solar, wind and battery storage projects in Australia, France, Finland, the US, Mexico and elsewhere, with over 9 GW in operation or construction. It sells electricity to utilities and corporates under long-term contracts. Acquired by Brookfield Renewable and partners (including Canada's CPP Investments and Mubadala-linked capital) in 2024-25 for around EUR 6bn, and delisted from Euronext. B2B energy firm, little consumer awareness.

NEURA Robotics is a Metzingen, Germany robotics company, founded in 2019, making cognitive collaborative robots (the MAiRA and LARA arms) and humanoid robots such as 4NE1, with its Neuraverse platform. It supplies manufacturers and logistics firms, and has a partnership with Kawasaki and Schaeffler. A 2025 round raised about EUR 120m, with later funding reportedly pushing total capital near $1.7bn. Private. Prominent in European tech media, no mainstream consumer brand yet.

Nuro is a Mountain View, California autonomous driving company, founded in 2016, which built small self-driving delivery vehicles before switching to licensing the Nuro Driver technology to automakers and mobility partners. It has a deal with Uber and Lucid to deploy robotaxis. It has raised over $2bn, including a 2021 round that valued it near $8.6bn, from SoftBank, Google and Nvidia. Private. B2B technology brand with moderate awareness in automotive circles.

OpenText is a Waterloo, Ontario enterprise information management software company, selling content management, cybersecurity, analytics, AI and business network products to large enterprises and governments. It grew through acquisitions including Micro Focus (2023) and Carbonite, with revenue near $5bn and about 22,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (OTEX). B2B software company with little consumer awareness, though it has run F1-related and team technology partnerships.

Pinterest is a San Francisco visual discovery platform where users save and organise ideas as pins for shopping, recipes, home, fashion and travel. It has more than 570 million monthly active users and earns from advertising, with revenue near $4bn. Founded in 2010, it listed on the NYSE (PINS) in 2019. Strong consumer social brand with heavy use by women and Gen Z users, and advertiser-focused partnerships rather than sports sponsorship.

PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California quantum computing company building a fault-tolerant, utility-scale photonic quantum computer with silicon photonics chips manufactured with GlobalFoundries. It is constructing sites in Brisbane, Australia and Chicago, backed by government funding. It raised $1bn in 2025 at a valuation of $7bn from BlackRock, Temasek and Baillie Gifford, with total funding above $2.5bn. Private. Prominent in deep-tech, with no consumer products.

Ready Capital is a New York mortgage real estate investment trust and lender that originates and services small-balance commercial loans, SBA 7(a) loans, and multifamily and investor loans, with a large servicing portfolio. Customers are small businesses and property investors. Listed on the NYSE (RC), externally managed by Waterfall Asset Management. B2B finance firm with no consumer brand.

Reflection AI is a New York frontier AI lab, founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, working on autonomous coding agents and open frontier models. It raised $2bn in October 2025 at an $8bn valuation, led by Nvidia, with 1789 Capital, Lightspeed and others, and is building up open-weight model releases. Private. Known in AI circles, with no consumer products yet.

Riot Platforms is a Bitcoin miner based in Castle Rock, Colorado, operating large mining facilities in Rockdale and Corsicana, Texas, plus engineering and data center hosting businesses. It earns by mining Bitcoin and by selling power flexibility to the Texas grid, and holds a large Bitcoin treasury. Listed on Nasdaq (RIOT). B2B and investor-oriented crypto firm, with no consumer brand but some visibility in crypto sponsorship.

Saronic is an Austin, Texas defence technology company building autonomous surface vessels and naval drones for the US Navy and allies, including the Corsair and Marauder vessels, and Port Alpha shipyard in Louisiana. Founded in 2022, it raised $600m in 2025 at a valuation of about $4bn, with later funding reportedly valuing it at around $9bn, from Elad Gil, 8VC, Andreessen Horowitz and others. Private. Government B2B, known in defence tech; not a consumer brand.

SentinelOne is a Mountain View, California cybersecurity company selling its AI-powered Singularity platform for endpoint, cloud, identity and security data protection to businesses and governments worldwide. It reports annual recurring revenue of around $1bn and thousands of customers. Listed on the NYSE (S) since 2021. B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though it has been active in sports sponsorship.

Silicon Box is a Singapore-based advanced semiconductor packaging company, founded in 2021, which builds chiplet integration and panel-level packaging for AI, high-performance computing and mobile customers. It runs a foundry in Singapore with a plant in Novara, Italy under development, backed by an EU-supported investment of EUR 3.2bn. Investors include Temasek and Sequoia. Private. B2B manufacturer, with no consumer visibility.

SiTime is a Santa Clara, California fabless chip company making MEMS-based silicon timing devices, including oscillators and clock generators, which replace quartz crystals in data centers, AI servers, automotive, industrial and mobile products. Customers are electronics and telecom equipment makers. Listed on Nasdaq (SITM), it was founded in 2003 and was held by MegaChips before its 2019 IPO. B2B component supplier, no consumer awareness.

Skild AI is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania robotics AI start-up, formed in 2023 by Carnegie Mellon roboticists, developing a general-purpose robot brain, Skild Brain, to run on many robot types. It raised about $1.4bn in a January 2026 round at a valuation near $14bn, with SoftBank, Nvidia and Macquarie, and earlier backing from Amazon and Lightspeed. Private. Known in AI and robotics circles; no consumer products.

STORE Capital was a Scottsdale, Arizona net-lease REIT owning single-tenant operational real estate such as restaurants, health clubs, schools and manufacturing sites, rented to mid-sized businesses. It was acquired in 2023 for about $14bn by GIC and Oak Street Real Estate Capital (Blue Owl) and delisted from the NYSE (STOR). Now privately owned and issuing debt. Landlord business with no consumer brand.
