Symrise is a Holzminden, Germany supplier of fragrances, flavours, cosmetic ingredients and pet food ingredients, serving consumer product makers across perfume, personal care, food and beverage and pet food. Revenue is about EUR 5bn with over 12,000 employees. Its brands include Diana Pet Food. Listed in Frankfurt (SY1) in the DAX/MDAX. B2B ingredient firm, so low consumer awareness, though its customers are major consumer brands.

Tabby is a Riyadh-based buy-now-pay-later and fintech company serving the Gulf, with the app offering pay-in-4, instalments, cards and a shopping app across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait. Founded in the UAE in 2019, it raised $160m in 2025 at a $3.3bn valuation and later reached about $4.5bn in a secondary sale, with Blue Pool, Wellington, PayPal Ventures and others. Private, with a Saudi IPO plan. Strong Gulf consumer brand with heavy advertising and sports sponsorship.

Tempus AI is a Chicago health technology company providing genomic sequencing, clinical data and AI tools for precision medicine, serving oncologists, hospitals and pharma companies running drug development. It holds one of the largest clinical-molecular data libraries, with revenue near $1bn. Founded by Eric Lefkofsky, it listed on Nasdaq (TEM) in June 2024. Mostly B2B and clinician-facing, with modest direct consumer awareness.

Tenable is a Columbia, Maryland cybersecurity company known for the Nessus vulnerability scanner and its Tenable One exposure management platform, covering cloud, identity, operational technology and attack surface. Customers are over 40,000 organizations, including a large part of the Fortune 500, with revenue near $1bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TENB). B2B, with strong awareness in security teams and no consumer brand.

Thinking Machines Lab is a San Francisco AI research and product company founded in 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, with co-founders including John Schulman. It focuses on collaborative AI systems and released Tinker, a fine-tuning product. It raised $2bn in seed funding in 2025 at a $12bn valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Nvidia and AMD, and has been reported as raising more at a much higher valuation. Private. Heavily covered in tech media; no consumer products yet.

Thomson Reuters is a Toronto-based information and technology company providing legal research (Westlaw), tax and accounting software, news (Reuters) and trade compliance tools to professionals, corporations and governments. It earns subscription revenue of about US$7.3bn and employs about 26,000 people. Majority-controlled by the Thomson family through Woodbridge. Listed on the TSX and Nasdaq (TRI). Mostly B2B, though the Reuters news agency is a globally known brand and it sponsors some events.

TIAA (Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America) is a New York financial services group offering retirement plans, annuities, wealth management and asset management (Nuveen) mainly to people in academic, medical, research and government fields. It manages over $1.3 trillion in assets, organised as a non-profit-linked mutual-style company. Funding shown reflects capital raises. Established brand among US teachers and non-profit staff; it has sponsored sport in the past.

TTM Technologies is a Santa Ana, California manufacturer of printed circuit boards, RF components and assemblies serving aerospace and defence, data center and networking, automotive and medical customers, with plants in North America and Asia. Revenue is about $2.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TTMI). B2B supplier with no consumer awareness.

Wayve is a London autonomous driving company, founded in 2017, developing end-to-end AI driving software that learns from data rather than high-definition maps. It tests vehicles in the UK, US, Germany and Japan, trialled robotaxis with Uber, and has a deal with Nissan for its ProPilot system. It raised $1.05bn in 2024 (led by SoftBank, with Nvidia and Microsoft) and later raised more, with total funding of about $2.5bn. Private. Well known in tech and mobility circles, with no consumer products yet.

Yondr Group is a London-headquartered developer, owner and operator of hyperscale data centers, building campuses for cloud and technology customers in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. It was acquired by DigitalBridge in 2021 and later partnered with Ardian. Revenue comes from long-term data center leases. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

Abercrombie and Kent is a global luxury travel company, founded in 1962 by Geoffrey Kent in Kenya, offering private journeys, safaris, cruises and small-group tours in over 100 countries, with offices worldwide and a US base in Downers Grove, Illinois. Customers are affluent leisure travellers, earning revenue from tour and trip bookings. Privately held, with investors including Dubai-based and US capital. A premium travel brand with strong awareness among high-net-worth travellers.

American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) is a New York corporate travel management company providing booking tools, expense management and meetings services to businesses, with acquisition of CWT in 2025. It serves thousands of corporate clients in over 140 countries and earns transaction fees. Listed on the NYSE (GBTG) since a 2022 SPAC, with American Express, Qatar Investment Authority and Juweel as major holders. B2B, well known to travel buyers, with the Amex-linked brand partly visible.

BeyonCa is described by Crunchbase as a Beijing-based manufacturer of electric vehicles with advanced features, and the input lists manufacturing as its industry. Funding shown is about CNY 10bn with the latest round in October 2023. The input gives no further detail on models, owners or sales volumes. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Blinkit (formerly Grofers) is a Gurugram quick-commerce platform delivering groceries, electronics and household goods to customers in around 10 minutes from dark stores across hundreds of Indian cities. It earns product margin, delivery and advertising revenue. Acquired by Zomato in 2022, now part of Eternal Ltd, which is listed on the NSE and BSE. Strong urban consumer brand in India with heavy advertising, including around cricket.

Bloomin' Brands is a Tampa, Florida restaurant group operating Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse, with about 1,450 restaurants in the US, Brazil and other international markets, including franchises. Revenue is about $4bn. Listed on Nasdaq (BLMN). Strong casual dining consumer brands, especially Outback in the US and Brazil, and a regular sports sponsor and advertiser.

Carro is a Singapore-headquartered online used car marketplace and automotive platform operating in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong and Taiwan, combining car sales, financing, insurance, subscriptions and an auction business. Founded in 2012, it became a unicorn in 2021 and has raised over $1.1bn including debt, with backers like SoftBank and Temasek. Private. Strong consumer brand in Singapore and nearby markets, with significant marketing spend.

ENOVATE Motors is described by Crunchbase as an automotive industry company based in Shanghai, China, with the input listing automotive, energy and mobility among its industries. Funding shown is about CNY 7.75bn with the latest round in March 2023. The input gives no more detail on its vehicles, customers or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Flink is a Berlin-based quick-commerce grocery delivery company, delivering groceries in minutes from dark stores in Germany, the Netherlands and Austria. It earns product margins and delivery fees from urban consumers, and has raised about $1.5bn including a 2022 round led by REWE and Mubadala at a $2.1bn valuation. REWE Group is its largest shareholder. Private. Consumer brand with solid awareness in German cities, though with modest advertising budgets.

Ford Otosan is a Turkish vehicle manufacturer based in Kocaeli, a joint venture between Ford Motor Company and the Koc Group, each holding about 41 percent. It makes the Transit and Puma family, Courier and heavy trucks including the F-MAX, at plants in Golcuk, Yeniköy and Craiova (Romania), plus a growing EV business. It exports across Europe. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (FROTO). Leading brand in Turkey's commercial vehicle market, with F1 and Ford-linked marketing exposure.

Hindustan Urvarak and Rasayan Limited (HURL) is a New Delhi-based fertilizer maker formed as a joint venture of NTPC, Coal India, Indian Oil and the Fertilizer Corporation of India and Hindustan Fertilizer Corporation to revive urea plants at Gorakhpur, Sindri and Barauni. Customers are Indian farmers supplied through government distribution, funded by central subsidies. State-linked and privately held, with funding shown at INR 128bn. B2B and government-linked, with no consumer brand.

inKind is an Austin, Texas fintech that gives diners rewards and financing for dining out, working with restaurants to offer credit to spend at their venues and rewards in return, run through the inKind app. Restaurants get working capital and marketing, and diners receive discounts. Launched in 2017, it has raised about $1.2bn including debt facilities, with investors such as Matrix Partners and Valar Ventures. Private. Known among US foodies and restaurateurs.

Marex is a London-based global commodities and financial markets services group (shown with a New York address), providing brokerage, clearing, hedging, market making and trading across energy, metals, agriculture and foreign exchange for corporates and institutions. Revenue is about $1.7bn. It listed on Nasdaq (MRX) in April 2024. B2B financial group with little consumer awareness, although it has made sponsorship moves in sport.

MBRF is the Brazilian food group formed in 2025 by the merger of Marfrig and BRF, headquartered in Sao Paulo. Its brands include Sadia, Perdigao, Qualy, Bassi and Marfrig, covering beef, chicken, pork, processed and plant-based foods, selling in Brazil and over 140 countries, with revenue above BRL 150bn and a workforce of about 150,000. Listed on B3 (MBRF3). Strong consumer brands in Brazil, and Sadia and Perdigao have a long history of football sponsorship.

PODS is a Clearwater, Florida portable moving and storage company that delivers storage containers to homes and businesses, then picks them up and moves or stores them, operating in the US, Canada and Australia. Founded in 1998, it earns from container rentals, moves and storage, and uses franchise and licensee partners. Owned by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan since 2021. Private. Recognisable consumer-facing brand in North America with mass-market advertising.

QVC is a Rocky Mount, North Carolina (corporate base West Chester, Pennsylvania) video and online retailer, selling home, fashion, beauty, jewellery and electronics through TV shopping channels and digital platforms in the US, UK, Germany, Japan and Italy. It is a subsidiary of Qurate Retail, and its sister brand HSN is also part of the group. Revenue runs near $10bn. Qurate is listed on Nasdaq (QRTEA). Well-known consumer shopping brand with an older, primarily female audience.

ROX Motor is described by Crunchbase as a Shanghai-based car-making project focusing on off-road electric vehicles, with industries listed as automotive and electric vehicles. Funding shown is about $1.38bn with the latest round in September 2023. The input gives no more detail on models, sales or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Summit Hotel Properties is a hotel real estate investment trust, based in Austin, Texas with an input address elsewhere in California, owning upscale select-service hotels under Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt brands such as Courtyard, Hampton Inn and Hyatt Place in the US. Revenue comes from hotel operations. Listed on the NYSE (INN). Property owner; guests see the franchise brands rather than Summit, so consumer awareness is low.

The Very Group is a Liverpool-based digital retailer and financial services company running the Very online store and the Littlewoods brand, selling fashion, homewares, electronics and toys on interest-bearing buy-now-pay-later credit to UK customers. Revenue is around GBP 2bn, with about 5 million active customers. Owned by the Barclay family trust, with Very Financial Services as a core earner. Private. Strong UK consumer brand with heavy advertising, and has sponsored football.

Transat A.T. is a Montreal-based integrated Canadian tour operator and airline group, selling vacation packages, flights and hotel stays to destinations in the Caribbean, Europe and Mexico under Air Transat and the Transat travel brand, with offices in Canada, France and the UK. Revenue is about C$2.9bn. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TRZ). Strong Canadian consumer travel brand, with Air Transat well known in Quebec and across Canada.

Travelport is a global travel technology company, based in Langley, Berkshire, whose distribution platform connects airlines, hotels and car rental firms to travel agencies and online booking sites. It earns transaction fees from bookings, and in 2019 was taken private by Siris Capital and Elliott. The company later combined with others and carries a sizeable debt load. Private. B2B travel platform, with no consumer brand awareness.

Vroom was a Houston, Texas online used car retailer that sold vehicles directly to consumers with delivery to the door. It shut its ecommerce used-vehicle business in early 2024 and is now focused on its UACC auto lending unit, and parts of the company went through a prepackaged Chapter 11 restructuring in late 2024. Listed on Nasdaq (VRM) before the changes. A formerly well-advertised consumer brand, now largely a wound-down consumer finance business.

Zeekr is the premium electric vehicle brand of Geely Holding, based in Hangzhou, making models such as the Zeekr 001, 007, 009 MPV and X. It sells in China, Europe and other markets and listed on the NYSE (ZK) in 2024, then was taken private by Geely Automobile in a 2025 merger. Vehicle deliveries exceeded 200,000 a year. Strong Chinese premium EV brand, building awareness in Europe, with sponsorship activity in sport and F1-adjacent events.

A&O Hotels and Hostels is a Berlin-based budget hotel and hostel chain with around 40 locations in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, the Czech Republic, Italy, Denmark, Hungary and the UK, offering private rooms and dorm beds to young travellers, families and school groups. Founded in 2000, it earns room revenue from accommodation and is privately held with private equity backing. Reasonably known in Germany among budget travellers, with little profile elsewhere.

Aritzia is a Vancouver-based women's fashion retailer, designing everyday luxury apparel under brands such as Babaton, Wilfred, Sunday Best and TNA, sold through about 130 boutiques in Canada and the US plus online. Revenue is above C$3bn and it has grown fast in the US. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ATZ), with the Chiu family and Berkshire Partners investor in the past. Strong consumer fashion brand in Canada, with growing US awareness.

Arrival was a London-based electric vehicle maker, founded in 2015, which designed electric vans and buses built in micro-factories, with backing from Hyundai, Kia and UPS, and listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC in 2021. It ran out of money, and its UK arm entered administration in early 2024. Funding was about $1.0bn. Now defunct as a manufacturer, with no active commercial relevance.

Battersea Power Station is a London regeneration site on the Thames, a former coal-fired power station redeveloped into a mixed-use district with apartments, offices (Apple's UK headquarters), shops, restaurants, leisure venues and an events venue, with a Northern line station. It is owned by a Malaysian consortium of Sime Darby Property, SP Setia and the Employees Provident Fund. The input lists a funding amount of GBP 880m. Visitor-oriented property venue, with significant London consumer awareness.

Clearco is a Toronto fintech, formerly Clearbanc, that offers revenue-based financing to e-commerce and software companies, advancing cash for marketing and inventory in exchange for a share of future revenue. It restructured in 2022-23, cutting staff and exiting several markets. Funding of about $960m includes equity and debt. Private. B2B fintech known to online merchants, with no consumer brand awareness.

Global Eggs is a privately owned holding group from Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil, that operates in egg production and egg products for the consumer goods and food industry, according to Crunchbase. The input shows funding of about $1bn with the latest round in March 2026. No further detail on brands, scale or ownership is given. Food manufacturing supplier. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Golden Goose is a Milan-based Italian luxury footwear and fashion brand, famed for its pre-distressed hand-finished Super-Star sneakers, plus Ball Star, apparel and accessories, sold through boutiques, e-commerce and department stores in Europe, North America and Asia. Revenue is about EUR 600m. Owned by Permira, which bought it from Carlyle in 2020, with Hillhouse-led co-investors. Private, with a possible IPO. Strong luxury-fashion brand among younger affluent buyers.

Hyundai Mobis is a Seoul-based South Korean auto parts maker, the largest supplier to Hyundai Motor Group, producing modules (chassis, cockpit, front-end), electrification parts, ADAS sensors, lamps and aftermarket parts, with global sales near KRW 60 trillion. It also runs a Mobis parts aftersales business. Listed on the Korea Exchange (012330), with Hyundai-affiliated groups as major shareholders. Mostly B2B, known to the auto industry, with limited consumer brand awareness.

Las Vegas Sands is a Las Vegas-based resort developer and operator of integrated casino resorts. It sold its Las Vegas properties, the Venetian and Palazzo, in 2022 and now focuses on Singapore (Marina Bay Sands) and Macau (The Venetian Macao, The Londoner, The Parisian). Revenue is around $11bn, earned from gaming, hotel, retail, convention and entertainment. Listed on the NYSE (LVS), controlled by the Adelson family. Marina Bay Sands is an iconic Singapore landmark with strong travel brand visibility.

Melia Hotels International is a Palma de Mallorca-based Spanish hotel group, one of the largest holiday hotel operators in the world, running around 400 hotels in about 40 countries under Melia, Gran Melia, ME, Paradisus, Innside and Sol brands, strong in Spain, the Caribbean and Latin America. Revenue is about EUR 2bn. Listed on the Spanish stock exchange (MEL), with the Escarrer family in control. Strong consumer brand in Spanish-speaking markets and a sponsor of sports.

Quince is a San Francisco direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand selling apparel (cashmere, silk, linen), homeware, leather goods, jewellery and bedding at lower prices by cutting out the middleman. Customers are mainly US online shoppers, with expansion into Europe. Founded in 2018, it raised $500m in 2025 at a $4.5bn valuation. Private. Growing consumer brand with heavy social-media advertising, and a growing sports and media sponsorship presence.

Vishal Mega Mart is an Indian value retail chain, based in Gurugram, running over 600 department-style stores in tier 2 and tier 3 cities selling apparel, general merchandise and fast-moving consumer goods, much of it under its own private labels. Serving middle- and lower-income households, it earns from retail sales and has an online channel. Controlled by Kedaara Capital and Partners Group (after Temasek's earlier ownership), it listed on the NSE and BSE in December 2024. Strong value-retail brand in India with modest national advertising.

YTO Express is a Shanghai-based Chinese express parcel delivery company, one of the country's largest couriers, handling billions of parcels a year for e-commerce sellers and consumers through a network of franchised outlets and sorting hubs. It earns delivery fees and is part of the Alibaba-linked courier ecosystem, and its parent is Yuantong Express. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600233). B2B and B2C logistics brand, well known in China, with little profile abroad.

Blue Bird Corporation is a Macon, Georgia manufacturer of school buses, including Type A, C and D buses, plus electric, propane and CNG versions, with a strong share of the US and Canadian school bus market. Customers are school districts, contractors and transit agencies, and revenue is about $1.3bn. Listed on Nasdaq (BLBD). Founded in 1927. B2B and institutional manufacturer, the yellow bus is iconic but the corporate brand has low direct consumer awareness. Crunchbase country is shown as Georgia (the US state).

DST Car (Shenzhen Dongshangtong, Dingshentong) is a Chinese new energy vehicle rental and mobility platform based in Shenzhen, operating electric car and ride-hailing fleet leasing to drivers and consumers across Chinese cities. It earns lease and rental income. Funding is about $729m, with backers including Chinese investment funds. Private. Business-to-driver service with a regional consumer audience in China and no international brand.

Getaround is a Paris-founded car-sharing marketplace, now US-based after a 2022 SPAC merger, letting owners rent out vehicles to drivers through its app with keyless access, in cities in the US and Europe. It earns a share of rental fees and insurance. It was listed on the NYSE (GETR) and exited the US market in early 2025, wound down parts of its business and focuses on Europe. Funding about $763m. A consumer-facing mobility app with modest awareness.

Horse Powertrain is a London-registered powertrain company formed in 2022 as a joint venture between Renault Group and Geely, with Aramco joining as a 10 percent investor in 2024. It builds combustion engines, hybrid systems and transmissions, with plants and R&D in Europe, Brazil, China and Turkey, and about 19,000 employees. Customers include Renault, Dacia, Geely brands and other carmakers. B2B component maker, with the Horse name known in the car industry only.

JSW Motors is the automotive arm of India's JSW Group, based in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra, set up to build electric and new-energy vehicles in India, including a tie-up to market MG-branded cars through JSW MG Motor, formerly SAIC-owned MG Motor India. It plans a large new factory with investment of about INR 80bn. Part of the JSW conglomerate led by Sajjan Jindal. Early-stage brand with growing but limited consumer awareness; JSW is a notable Indian sports sponsor.

Rimac Group is a Croatian electric hypercar and technology company based near Zagreb, formed from Rimac Automobili (maker of the Nevera) and Bugatti Rimac, which owns Bugatti, and Rimac Technology, a supplier of battery systems and drivetrains for carmakers such as Porsche, Aston Martin and Koenigsegg. Founded by Mate Rimac in 2009, its investors include Porsche (about 45 percent) and Hyundai/Kia. Private. Very high profile among car enthusiasts, with its hypercar sales limited to a few hundred units.

Dongchedi (Car Home competitor) is the Chinese automotive information and car-buying platform from ByteDance, offering reviews, pricing, live-streams, videos and lead generation for car dealers and automakers, with a mobile app and Douyin integration. It earns advertising and lead fees from automakers and dealers. Part of ByteDance, which is privately held, with about $600m funding listed. Strong brand among Chinese car shoppers, very little outside China.

Kyte is a San Francisco company, founded in 2020, that delivers rental cars to customers' doors in US cities through a driver handover app, with a marketplace focus on convenience and subscription flexibility. It earns rental and delivery fees and has been backed by Chicago-based and other investors. Funding shown is about $549m including debt. Private. Small consumer mobility brand with limited national awareness.

Plastic Omnium (rebranded OPmobility in 2024) is a French automotive supplier based in Levallois-Perret, making exterior body parts, bumpers, fuel and hydrogen storage systems, lighting, and e-mobility systems for car makers worldwide, with revenue near EUR 11bn and about 40,000 employees. Controlled by Burelle SA and the Burelle family. Listed on Euronext Paris (OPM). B2B supplier, with brand known to the auto industry rather than consumers.

Spiro (Spironet) is a Nairobi-linked, Africa-focused electric motorcycle and battery-swap company, founded in Benin and growing in Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Togo and Nigeria, selling electric motorcycles and swap networks to boda-boda taxi riders and delivery fleets. Funding is about $575m according to Crunchbase. Private, backed by Afreximbank, Equator and others. Growing brand among African commercial riders, with little international consumer awareness.

Allison Transmission Holdings is an Indianapolis maker of fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles, buses, fire trucks, defence vehicles and off-highway equipment, along with electrified propulsion systems. It sells to truck and bus makers and the military, with revenue of about $3bn and plants in Indiana and Hungary and India. Listed on the NYSE (ALSN). B2B supplier; the brand is known to fleet operators but not to consumers.

AMAG Leasing is the automotive leasing and financing arm of the AMAG Group, Switzerland's largest car importer and dealer, based in Cham, Zug. It leases and finances Volkswagen, Audi, SEAT, Skoda and other vehicles to private customers and businesses in Switzerland. AMAG Group is privately owned by the Haefner family. Funding shown is CHF 450m. Local B2B2C finance brand with limited visibility outside Switzerland.

ECD Automotive Design is a Kissimmee, Florida company that restores and customises classic Land Rover Defenders and Range Rovers, and since 2024 other vehicles, as bespoke luxury builds, sometimes with electric conversions, with prices well into six figures. It builds vehicles for wealthy individual clients and shows them on social media and TV. Listed on the NYSE (ECDA) in 2023 via a SPAC merger. Niche premium brand with strong social-media following among car enthusiasts.

Global Lending Services (GLS) is a US auto finance company serving consumers with subprime or near-prime vehicle loans and leases through dealers, with offices in Greenville, South Carolina and Atlanta. It earns interest and fees on loans, funded through debt facilities of about $500m. Private. B2B2C lender known to dealers, with little consumer brand awareness. Limited public detail beyond the input.

Zero Motorcycles is a Scotts Valley, California maker of electric motorcycles, including the SR/F, SR/S and DS lines, sold through dealers in North America, Europe and Asia to consumers, as well as to police and fleets. Founded in 2006 by Neal Saiki, it has raised hundreds of millions from investors such as Invus and Mahindra-linked backers. Private. Known among motorcycle enthusiasts, with a modest brand presence.

Chunqing Technology is described by Crunchbase as a Chinese company creating a new generation of electric vehicles, listed as based in Tianjin, with Guangdong appearing in the location field. The input lists automotive and electric vehicle industries and funding of about $435m with the latest round in July 2025. No more detail on products, customers or owners is given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Garmin is a GPS technology company, legally Swiss and operating from Olathe, Kansas, making GPS wearables and smartwatches (Forerunner, fenix, Venu), cycling computers, marine electronics, aviation avionics, automotive navigation and in-car systems. It sells to consumers and OEM customers worldwide, with revenue near $7bn and about 20,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (GRMN). Strong consumer brand among athletes, pilots and boaters, and a sports sponsor including sailing, cycling and motorsport.

Vertelo is an Indian fleet electrification and EV leasing platform based in Mumbai, backed by Mahindra Group's venture and others, offering electric vehicles on lease or financing to delivery and mobility fleets without upfront ownership cost. It earns lease income and services, and arranged about $400m including debt. Private. B2B fleet finance brand, known to logistics operators and little to consumers.

AirTrunk is an Australian hyperscale data center operator, founded in 2014 by Robin Khuda and based in Sydney, with campuses across Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia and Indonesia, serving cloud and AI customers such as Microsoft, Google and Alibaba. It was acquired in 2024 by Blackstone and CPP Investments for about A$24bn. Revenue is earned from long-term data center capacity contracts. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

E.ON is an Essen-based German energy group and Europe's largest operator of electricity distribution networks, also selling power, gas and energy solutions to tens of millions of customers in Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, Sweden, Italy, Romania and elsewhere. Revenue is about EUR 80bn with over 70,000 employees. Listed in Frankfurt (EOAN) in the DAX. Familiar consumer utility brand in Germany and a sponsor of football and other sports, including its E.ON Cup partnerships.

Iliad is a French telecom group, founded by Xavier Niel and based in Paris, behind the Free mobile and broadband brand in France, plus Iliad Italia, Play in Poland and a stake in other operators. It serves over 50 million subscribers, with revenue around EUR 11bn, and owns data center and fibre assets, including OpCore. Privately held, controlled by Niel's holding after delisting in 2018. Free is a strong disruptive consumer brand in France.

Kroger is the largest traditional supermarket operator in the US, headquartered in Cincinnati, running about 2,700 stores under banners such as Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer, Harris Teeter and King Soopers, plus fuel centres, pharmacies and private-label brands like Simple Truth. Annual sales are near $150bn with around 410,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (KR). Its attempt to merge with Albertsons failed in 2024. Very high US consumer awareness; it sponsors sports and community events regionally.

MTR Corporation operates Hong Kong's metro network and rail services, plus railways in mainland China, London (Elizabeth line), Stockholm, Sydney and Melbourne, and earns from fares, property development and station retail. It carries millions of passengers a day. Majority-owned by the Hong Kong government, with an HQ in Kowloon, and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (0066). Ubiquitous brand to Hong Kong commuters with strong local awareness, and a sponsor of local events.

Phoenix Tower International is a Boca Raton, Florida owner and operator of wireless communications towers, with thousands of sites in Latin America, Europe, Africa and Asia leased to mobile network operators. It earns long-term tenancy revenue. Owned by Blackstone since 2016, which bought it for infrastructure investment. Private. B2B infrastructure, with no consumer visibility.

Switch is a Las Vegas data center and technology infrastructure company, with large campuses in Nevada, Georgia, Michigan and Texas and Europe and Asia, known for its SUPERNAP facilities and Tahoe Reno park. Customers include cloud, tech and enterprise firms. It was taken private in 2022 by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors for about $11bn. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness, though it has been involved in Las Vegas sports and naming deals.

Tsinghua Unigroup was a Chinese state-backed semiconductor and technology conglomerate, with a base in Beijing, owned by Tsinghua Holdings, which includes memory-chip firm YMTC, mobile chip designer Unisoc and server group H3C. It defaulted on bonds in 2020 and went through a bankruptcy restructuring in 2021-22 and was bought by a consortium led by Wise Road Capital and Jianguang Asset Management. A B2B chip group with big strategic importance in China and no consumer brand.

Verizon is a US telecom giant, based in Basking Ridge, New Jersey, serving about 145 million mobile and broadband connections with wireless, Fios fibre, 5G home internet and business services. It earns subscription fees and has revenue near $135bn. Listed on the NYSE and Nasdaq (VZ). Very strong consumer brand and a major sports sponsor, notably as an NFL partner and in IndyCar. Funding figure shown reflects debt raised rather than venture equity.

Vodafone Group is a London-headquartered telecom operator, offering mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise connectivity in Europe and Africa, including Vodafone Germany, Vodafone UK (merged with Three), Vodacom in South Africa and the M-Pesa mobile money service. Revenue is about EUR 37bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (VOD) and Nasdaq. Very recognisable consumer brand, and a former Formula 1 sponsor (McLaren, 2001-2013), now a sponsor in sports and arts.

Amer Sports is a sporting goods group, now headquartered in Helsinki and listed on the NYSE (AS), owning brands including Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Atomic, Peak Performance and Armada. Revenue is about $6bn. Owned mainly by Chinese investors led by Anta Sports and FountainVest, which bought it in 2019. It sells apparel, footwear and equipment to consumers through retail, wholesale and e-commerce worldwide. Strong consumer brands, particularly Arc'teryx and Salomon, and a regular sports sponsor.

AST SpaceMobile is a Midland, Texas company building a space-based cellular broadband network of large low-earth-orbit satellites that connect directly to ordinary smartphones. Partners include AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone and Rakuten, and it has launched its BlueBird satellites. It earns revenue from wholesale service with mobile operators and government deals. Listed on Nasdaq (ASTS) after a 2021 SPAC merger. Pre-commercial technology company, with growing investor awareness but no consumer brand.

Brightspeed is a Charlotte, North Carolina broadband provider formed in 2022 when Apollo Global bought Lumen Technologies' local telephone and consumer fibre assets in 20 states, and it is building fibre to millions of homes in rural and suburban areas of the US. It serves residential and business customers, earning subscription fees. Private, with funding of over $6.5bn through debt and equity from Apollo. Regional consumer broadband brand, with limited awareness.

Bunge is a St. Louis-area (Chesterfield, Missouri) global agribusiness and food ingredient company that buys, stores, processes and trades oilseeds and grains such as soybeans, corn and wheat, and sells vegetable oils, flour, meal and sugar. In 2025 it completed its purchase of Viterra. Customers are food producers, feed makers and biofuel firms worldwide, and revenue is about $50-60bn. Listed on the NYSE (BG). B2B commodity group with low consumer awareness.

Canadian National Railway (CN) is a Montreal-based freight railroad running about 19,500 route miles across Canada and down to the US Gulf Coast, hauling intermodal containers, grain, coal, forest products, petroleum and automobiles. Revenue is around C$17bn with about 24,000 employees. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (CNR/CNI) and widely held, with Bill Gates a notable investor. B2B freight railway with strong Canadian industry recognition but little consumer awareness.

CPKC (Canadian Pacific Kansas City) is a Calgary-based railway created in 2023 when Canadian Pacific acquired Kansas City Southern, forming the only single-line rail network connecting Canada, the US and Mexico. It moves grain, automotive, intermodal, energy and industrial goods and also runs the CPKC Holiday Train. Revenue is about C$14bn. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (CP). B2B freight railway, with a mid-level public profile in Canada.

Delek Logistics Partners is a Brentwood, Tennessee master limited partnership that owns pipelines, terminals, storage and trucking assets, handling crude oil and refined products mainly for its sponsor Delek US Holdings, in Texas, Arkansas, Tennessee and other states. It earns fee-based revenue and pays distributions to unit holders. Listed on the NYSE (DKL). B2B midstream, no consumer brand.

Deutsche Glasfaser is a Dusseldorf-based German fibre-to-the-home network operator building and running gigabit fibre in mostly rural and small-town areas, selling broadband to households and wholesale access to other providers. Owned by EQT Infrastructure and OMERS, which committed billions of euros of financing for its rollout. Private. Consumer-facing in its regions with local advertising, and recognisable among German broadband buyers.

EdgeConneX is a Herndon, Virginia data center developer and operator that builds edge and hyperscale facilities in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific for cloud providers, content companies and enterprises. It has been owned by EQT Infrastructure since 2018, which took over from Providence Equity. Private, with funding mainly debt. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Edgecore Digital Infrastructure is described by Crunchbase as an experienced global data center company based in Denver, Colorado, with industries listed under information technology. Funding shown is about $3.1bn with the latest round in October 2026. No further detail on campuses, customers or owners is given in the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ESR Group is a pan-Asia-Pacific logistics real estate developer, owner and fund manager based in Singapore (with Hong Kong operations), with a portfolio of warehouses and data centers and fund management of over $150bn of assets. Customers are e-commerce, retail and logistics tenants, and income comes from rent, development and fees. Taken private in 2025 by a consortium including Starwood Capital, Warburg Pincus and Sixth Street, after Hong Kong listing (1821). B2B property, no consumer profile.

Ferguson is a Newport News, Virginia (US-listed) wholesale distributor of plumbing, heating, HVAC, waterworks and building products, serving residential and commercial contractors in the US and Canada from over 1,700 locations. Revenue is about $30bn. Once part of Wolseley UK, it moved its primary listing to the NYSE (FERG) in 2022. B2B distributor, known to trade professionals, with low consumer awareness.

FiberCop is an Italian broadband network company based in Milan, created in 2021 from TIM's fixed-access network and FiberCop assets, now serving as Italy's main fibre and copper access network, wholesale to telecom operators. It is owned by KKR (about 37.5 percent) with TIM, Fastweb and F2i. After acquiring TIM's network, it is ultimately controlled by KKR following a 2024 deal. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer visibility.

Fleet Data Centers is described by Crunchbase as a data infrastructure company based in Denver, Colorado, with data center and data management industries. The input shows funding of about $8.4bn with the latest round in April 2026. It gives no more detail on its campuses, customers or backers, and similar names exist in the data center sector. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Goodman Group is an Australian industrial property group based in Sydney that owns, develops and manages logistics warehouses, business parks and increasingly data centers in Australia, New Zealand, Asia, Europe, the UK, North America and the Middle East. It manages billions of dollars of assets for institutional investors and earns development and fees income. Listed on the ASX (GMG). B2B real estate firm with no consumer brand awareness.

Huhtamaki is a Finnish packaging manufacturer, headquartered in Espoo, producing food and drink packaging such as paper cups, moulded fibre egg cartons, flexible packaging, labels and foodservice items for consumer goods and restaurant customers in more than 35 countries. Revenue is around EUR 4.1bn with about 17,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (HUH1V). B2B supplier; its products are everywhere in daily life but the brand is largely unknown to consumers.

International Distribution Services is the parent of Royal Mail and General Logistics Systems (GLS), a London-based postal and parcel group delivering letters and parcels in the UK and across Europe and Canada. It had revenue over GBP 12bn and about 140,000 employees. In 2025 it was acquired by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky's EP Group for about GBP 3.6bn and delisted from the London Stock Exchange. Royal Mail is a very well-known UK consumer brand.

Kinetic is the consumer and business brand of Windstream, based in Little Rock, Arkansas, providing high-speed internet, voice and data networking in rural and suburban areas of 18 US states, including fibre-to-the-home in many places. Windstream emerged from bankruptcy in 2020 under Elliott and Siris-held ownership, and merged with Uniti Group in 2025. Funding shown reflects debt. Regional broadband brand with low national awareness.

maincubes is a Frankfurt-based German data center operator and developer, part of the Zech Group, with campuses in Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Berlin and Vienna serving cloud, enterprise and carrier customers. It earns colocation and hyperscale rental income. Funding of about EUR 2.5bn reflects equity and debt capital raised. Private. B2B infrastructure with no consumer visibility.

Molson Coors is a Chicago-based global brewer, with brands Coors Light, Miller Lite, Molson Canadian, Blue Moon, Carling, Staropramen and Madri, selling in the US, Canada, Europe and other markets, with revenue near $11bn and about 16,000 employees. It also has a growing non-beer beverage portfolio. Listed on the NYSE (TAP). Very strong consumer brands, and a heavy long-running sports sponsor, including NHL, NFL and soccer.

Ocado Group is a British online grocery technology company, based in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, which developed a robotic warehouse and fulfilment system licensed to grocers such as Kroger, Coles, Aeon and Sobeys, and runs the Ocado Retail UK online supermarket with Marks and Spencer. Revenue from technology fees and retail is over GBP 3bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (OCDO). Ocado is a well-known UK consumer brand, though its technology business is B2B.

Ola (ANI Technologies) is a Bengaluru-based Indian ride-hailing company, with its core cab and auto-rickshaw app, and affiliates including Ola Electric (listed in 2024), Ola Financial Services and Ola Consumer. It serves tens of millions of riders in India. Backed by SoftBank, Tiger Global, Temasek and Matrix, and valued at about $7.3bn in 2021. Private. Very strong brand across Indian cities, with a history in cricket sponsorship, although it has been losing share to Uber and Rapido.

Optimum Communications is the 2025 rename of Altice USA, based in Bethpage, New York, a cable and broadband provider selling internet, TV, mobile and business services under Optimum and Suddenlink to about 4 million customers in 21 states, and the owner of News 12 and other media brands. Revenue is around $8.5bn and debt is very large. Listed on the NYSE (OPTU). Strong regional consumer brand, with sports media links in the New York area.

Princeton Digital Group is a Singapore-based data center developer and operator with campuses in Singapore, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Thailand serving cloud and internet customers. It is backed by Warburg Pincus and Macquarie Asset Management and has raised billions in equity and debt. Private, founded in 2017. B2B infrastructure, with no consumer awareness.

Prologis is the world's largest industrial real estate investment trust, based in San Francisco, owning and leasing roughly 1.3 billion square feet of logistics warehouses in 20 countries to retailers, e-commerce, third-party logistics and manufacturing firms such as Amazon. Revenue is around $8bn. It also builds data centers and energy projects. Listed on the NYSE (PLD). B2B landlord with low consumer awareness.

Prysmian Group is a Milan-based Italian cable maker, the world's largest by revenue, producing power transmission, submarine, building and telecom cables and optical fibre for utilities, offshore wind, data center and construction customers worldwide. Revenue is about EUR 17-18bn with over 30,000 employees. It acquired Encore Wire in the US in 2024. Listed on Borsa Italiana (PRY). B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

SBA Communications is a Boca Raton, Florida owner and operator of wireless towers, with about 40,000 sites across the US and Latin America leased to carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile. It earns recurring lease revenue, about $2.7bn per year, and is organised as a REIT. Listed on Nasdaq (SBAC). B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand profile.

Singtel is Singapore's largest telecom operator, majority-owned by Temasek, selling mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise ICT services in Singapore and through associates such as Optus (Australia), Airtel (India), Telkomsel (Indonesia) and Globe. It also invests in data centers via Nxera. Revenue is about S$14bn. Listed on the Singapore Exchange (Z74). Very strong consumer brand in Singapore, and a past title sponsor of the Singapore Grand Prix.

ST Telemedia Global Data Centres is a Singapore data center operator with facilities in Singapore, India, Indonesia, the UK, Ireland, the US and elsewhere, serving cloud, content and enterprise customers. It is majority-owned by ST Telemedia, which is part of Temasek, with KKR and Singtel acquiring a stake in 2025. Revenue comes from colocation and hyperscale leases. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

VEON is a Dubai-headquartered digital operator and telecom holding company, listed on Nasdaq (VEON), with mobile, digital financial services and entertainment businesses in Ukraine (Kyivstar), Pakistan (Jazz), Bangladesh (Banglalink) and Kazakhstan (Beeline Kazakhstan) after selling its Russian assets. It serves over 150 million customers. Revenue is about $4bn. Jazz and Kyivstar are strong consumer brands in their countries, with local sponsorship activity.

Vertiv is a Westerville, Ohio maker of critical digital infrastructure, supplying power, cooling, racks, thermal management and services to data centers, communications networks and industrial sites. Customers include hyperscalers, colocation providers and enterprises, with revenue near $9-10bn. It was formerly Emerson Network Power and listed on the NYSE (VRT) in 2020 via a SPAC with GS Acquisition Holdings. B2B brand, known in the data center industry, with little consumer awareness.

VodafoneZiggo is a Utrecht-based Dutch telecom operator, a 50-50 joint venture of Vodafone and Liberty Global formed in 2016, providing mobile, broadband, TV and business services to millions of customers in the Netherlands. Revenue is about EUR 4bn. Private, with debt financing. It operates Ziggo, Vodafone Netherlands and Ziggo Sport. Strong consumer brand in the Netherlands, with Ziggo Sport broadcasting Formula 1 locally and a sponsor of Dutch events.

Wolfspeed is a Durham, North Carolina maker of silicon carbide materials and power devices, used in electric vehicles, renewable energy, fast charging and industrial power, with wafer fabs in North Carolina and New York. It went through a Chapter 11 restructuring in 2025 and emerged with debt largely converted to equity. Customers include automakers and power electronics firms. Listed on the NYSE (WOLF). B2B semiconductor supplier with limited consumer awareness.

Zayo is a Denver-based fibre network and bandwidth provider operating long-haul and metro fibre across North America and Europe, selling dark fibre, wavelengths and Ethernet to carriers, hyperscalers and enterprises. It was taken private in 2020 by Digital Colony and EQT for about $14bn and agreed to acquire Crown Castle's fibre business in 2025. Private. B2B network provider, without consumer awareness.

Achieve is a Tempe, Arizona digital personal finance company, formed from the 2024 merger of Freedom Financial Network and Hanover Financial, offering debt consolidation loans, home equity loans and debt-settlement programmes to US consumers. It earns interest, fees and servicing income. Private. Known to US consumers who search for debt relief, mostly through direct-response marketing.

Agibank is a Brazilian digital bank, headquartered in Campinas, Sao Paulo, offering payroll loans, retiree-focused credit, personal loans, insurance and accounts, mainly to lower-income customers in Brazil, with a network of physical points of service. Funding shown is BRL 9.4bn. Private as of the input data. Consumer bank with solid regional awareness and growing marketing, including sports sponsorship in Brazil.

Avant is a Chicago-based online lender offering personal loans, credit cards and lending services to near-prime consumers across the US. It uses data models to underwrite borrowers and has issued billions of dollars in loans since 2012, also providing technology to bank partners. Backed by General Atlantic and Tiger Global, with debt facilities. Private. Consumer lender known through online marketing, with some local sports sponsorship.

Better.com (Better Home and Finance Holding) is a New York digital mortgage and home equity lender that lets US homebuyers apply online with AI tools, selling loans to investors. Founded in 2016 by Vishal Garg, its brand Better Mortgage expanded into insurance and real estate. It listed on Nasdaq (BETR) via a 2023 SPAC with Aurora Acquisition. SoftBank is an early investor. Consumer fintech with moderate awareness, and a past of controversy over layoffs.

CRED is a Bengaluru-based Indian fintech where users pay credit card bills and earn rewards, now offering loans, payments, UPI and commerce. Its members are mostly high-credit-score urban Indians. Founded in 2018 by Kunal Shah, it has raised about $1.8bn, valued around $3.5bn in a 2025 round after peaking at $6.4bn. Private. Strong brand recognition in India through celebrity-led advertising and cricket sponsorship.

CrossCountry Mortgage is a Cleveland, Ohio home lender, one of the largest retail mortgage originators in the US, with hundreds of branches across the country and a focus on purchase loans, including FHA, VA and conventional. It earns origination and servicing income. Privately held and led by founder Ron Wetherill. Known to homebuyers, with considerable sports marketing and sponsorship deals.

Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Toronto-based Canadian consumer lender offering personal loans, secured loans, home equity, retail financing and credit cards to near-prime customers through branches and online. It was formerly Fairstone Financial, part of the Duo Bank group. Private, with Birch Hill Equity Partners as an owner. Branch-based lender known to Canadian borrowers.

Huntington National Bank is the main banking subsidiary of Huntington Bancshares, based in Columbus, Ohio, offering consumer, small business, commercial and wealth banking across the Midwest and expanding into the South and West, with about $200bn in assets and over 1,000 branches. It has pursued acquisitions including Veritex and Cadence. Listed parent on Nasdaq (HBAN). Strong regional consumer brand and a visible sports and community sponsor.

Invited Clubs (formerly ClubCorp) is an Irving, Texas operator of private golf, country, athletic and city clubs, with about 200 clubs in the US, plus Invited Hospitality events. It earns membership dues, initiation fees and food and beverage revenue from members. Owned by Apollo Global Management, which bought ClubCorp in 2017 and rebranded it in 2021. Private. Upscale brand, recognised by golfers and affluent members, with some golf-related sponsorship activity.

Mister Car Wash is a Tucson, Arizona operator of about 500 car wash sites in the US, offering express exterior washes and a monthly Unlimited Wash Club membership with millions of members. Revenue is about $1bn. Listed on the NYSE (MCW), after a 2021 IPO, with Leonard Green and Apollo previously owning stakes. Consumer service brand with strong regional recognition and mass-market advertising.

OSRAM is the Munich-based lighting and semiconductor company, long a household name for light bulbs and automotive lighting, which became part of ams OSRAM in 2020 when Austria's ams AG acquired it for about EUR 4.6bn. It makes LEDs, lasers, sensors and automotive lamps (Osram and Sylvania brands). Customers are carmakers, electronics firms and consumers. Part of ams OSRAM (SIX: AMS). Well-known consumer lighting brand, especially in Germany.

PureGym is a Leeds-based low-cost gym operator, one of the largest in Europe, with around 600 sites and about 2 million members in the UK, Switzerland, Denmark, Saudi Arabia and Mexico. It earns monthly membership fees, with no contracts, and has expanded via acquisitions including Fitness Park in France. Owned by Leonard Green & Partners after buying it from KKR-backed owners in 2021. Private. Strong UK consumer brand with substantial advertising, including football partnerships.

San Diego Padres is the Major League Baseball franchise of San Diego, California, playing at Petco Park in the National League West. It earns from ticket sales, sponsorship, media rights and merchandising. Controlled by the Seidler family and partners after the death of Peter Seidler in 2023. Private. A large local fan base and a sports property that itself sells sponsorship inventory, rather than a corporate buyer.

Tencent Music Entertainment is a Shenzhen-based Chinese online music and audio group operating QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo and WeSing karaoke, and Ximalaya audio platform. It earns subscription and social entertainment revenue from hundreds of millions of users, with revenue near RMB 30bn. Controlled by Tencent Holdings and listed on the NYSE (TME) and Hong Kong (1698). Very strong consumer brand in China, with limited recognition outside China.

TMX Group is a Toronto-based Canadian financial exchange operator running the Toronto Stock Exchange, TSX Venture Exchange, Montreal Exchange and clearing houses, plus data and analytics (TMX Datalinx) and Trayport trading software. It earns listing fees, trading fees, and data subscription revenue, with revenue of roughly C$1.5bn. Listed on the TSX (X). B2B financial infrastructure, with high name recognition in Canadian finance but little consumer visibility.

VietJet Air is a Vietnamese low-cost airline founded by Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, based in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, flying domestic and international routes across Asia and beyond with an Airbus A320 family and A330 fleet and a large Boeing 737 MAX order. It carries tens of millions of passengers a year. Listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VJC). Strong consumer brand in Vietnam, known for flamboyant marketing, and an active sports sponsor.

Fireblocks is a New York digital asset infrastructure firm, founded in Israel in 2018, offering custody, wallet, transfer and tokenisation technology to banks, exchanges, payment firms and crypto businesses worldwide. It says it has secured trillions of dollars in transfers for over 2,000 customers. It raised $550m in 2022 at an $8bn valuation. Private. B2B crypto infrastructure, well known in digital asset circles but not to the public.

Repay (REPAY Holdings) is an Atlanta, Georgia electronic payment processing company providing integrated card and ACH processing, merchant acquiring and bill-pay software to businesses in niche verticals such as auto lending, consumer finance and healthcare. Revenue is near $300m. Listed on Nasdaq (RPAY) since a 2019 SPAC combination with Thunder Bridge. B2B fintech, with no consumer brand awareness. Crunchbase lists the country as Georgia (the US state).

Tabeo is a London-based UK fintech and payments company providing patient payment and contact management software, mainly for healthcare and professional service providers, according to Crunchbase's financial services and healthcare tags. Funding shown as 750m is probably a debt or facility figure in an unspecified currency. Private. B2B niche payments provider with little consumer awareness. Limited public detail beyond the input.

Bilt is a New York rewards and payments company that lets renters earn points on rent payments through the Bilt Mastercard, which has no fee for paying rent, and redeem them for travel, home and other rewards. It has over a million members and a $10.75bn valuation after a 2025 raise. Founded by Ankur Jain, with investors including General Catalyst, Valor and Left Lane. Private. Strong awareness among US renters and credit card enthusiasts.

Carmoola is a London-based UK car finance fintech that offers an online car loan marketplace and budget tool, letting consumers pre-approve finance in minutes and then buy from a dealer. It earns commission and interest, and has raised equity and debt facilities of about GBP 540m, backed by investors including Balderton and Illuminate. Private. Smaller consumer brand with growing awareness among UK car buyers.

Harness is a San Francisco software delivery platform, founded by Jyoti Bansal, that supplies AI-assisted CI/CD, feature flags, cloud cost management, security testing and internal developer portals to engineering teams. Customers include thousands of enterprises, and it raised $240m in 2025 at a $5.5bn valuation, with total funding of around $815m. Private. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness; sponsors some developer and sports events.

Match Group is a Dallas-based (listing shows Los Angeles) online dating company, operating Tinder, Hinge, Match.com, OkCupid, Plenty of Fish, Meetic and Azar, with tens of millions of paying users and revenue near $3.5bn from subscriptions and in-app purchases. Spun off from IAC in 2020 and listed on Nasdaq (MTCH). Very strong consumer brands, particularly Tinder and Hinge, and active in marketing and event partnerships.

ProCap Financial is a New York bitcoin treasury and financial services company launched in 2025, founded by Anthony Pompliano and merged with Columbus Circle Capital I, listed on Nasdaq (BRR). It holds bitcoin on its balance sheet and plans yield products and capital markets services, financed by a PIPE of more than $700m. Investor-facing vehicle, with moderate visibility in crypto circles and none to consumers.

United Nova Technology is described by Crunchbase as a company providing system manufacturing in electronics for the automotive industry, based in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, China. The input lists automotive and electronics industries and funding of about CNY 5.3bn with the latest round in September 2025. Products, customers and ownership are not stated. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

360 Finance (Qifu Technology) is a Shanghai-based Chinese digital consumer finance and credit technology company, spun out of Qihoo 360, connecting borrowers with financial institutions through its app and risk models. It earns platform and technology service fees on loan volumes. Listed on Nasdaq (QFIN). Consumer-facing fintech in China, with limited recognition outside the country.

ClickUp is a San Diego cloud work management platform for tasks, docs, chat, goals and AI tools, used by teams from start-ups to enterprises, with millions of users globally. It earns subscription fees and was valued at $4bn after a 2021 round, with total funding of about $660m from investors including Insight Partners, Craft and Tiger Global. Founded 2017. Private. Known to knowledge workers; B2B-leaning brand with low mainstream awareness.

Quantum Lending Solutions is a Reston, Virginia fintech providing AI-powered lending technology, according to Crunchbase, presumably serving lenders with digital loan origination and servicing tools. The input shows funding of about $658m with the latest round in November 2025. It is a private B2B vendor, with little consumer awareness. Limited detail on customers or ownership is available from the input.

Harbinger is a Garden Grove, California electric commercial vehicle maker, founded in 2022, building medium-duty electric truck chassis for delivery fleets, school buses and utility vehicles in the US, with Ford-linked backing. It raised about $358m in total, including a 2025 round. Private. B2B fleet supplier with low public awareness.

Hella is a Lippstadt, Germany automotive supplier of lighting, electronics and aftermarket parts, a century-old brand now majority-owned by Faurecia, which took control in 2022 and combined to form Forvia. Hella makes headlights, tail lights, sensors, ADAS radar and electronics for carmakers, plus a workshop-and-parts business. Part of Forvia (Euronext: FRVIA). Respected in the automotive trade, with limited direct consumer awareness; Hella has sponsored motorsport.

PC Jeweller is an Indian jewellery retailer, headquartered in Delhi, selling gold, diamond and silver jewellery through about 70 showrooms and an online presence. Founded by Padam Chand Gupta and run by his sons, it faced a severe debt crisis from 2018 with lender restructurings, and has since stabilised. Listed on the NSE and BSE (PCJEWELLER). A known regional jewellery brand in northern India, with modest advertising spend.

Tier IV is a Tokyo autonomous driving software company, founded in 2015, which develops and maintains the open-source Autoware platform and licenses self-driving software for buses, trucks and robotaxis. Investors include Yamaha Motor, Suzuki, Sompo and Sony-affiliated funds, and it works with Japanese cities and mobility operators. Private. B2B technology known in autonomous driving circles, with no consumer awareness.

Wallbox is a Barcelona-based maker of electric vehicle chargers, including home Pulsar units, public DC fast chargers and bidirectional chargers, plus energy management software, selling to consumers, businesses and utilities in Europe, North America and Asia. Revenue is about EUR 150m and losses are heavy. Listed on the NYSE (WBX) via a 2021 SPAC merger. Known to EV owners, with moderate consumer awareness.

Battery Smart is a Gurugram, India EV battery swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers, with hundreds of swap stations across Indian cities, mainly serving rickshaw and delivery drivers, who pay per swap. Founded in 2019, it raised about $285m including investments from Blume Ventures, Tiger Global, Trifecta Capital and Mahindra-linked funds. Private. Popular among commercial EV drivers, with low mainstream consumer awareness.

BlueStone is a Bengaluru-based Indian online-first fine jewellery brand, founded in 2011, selling certified gold and diamond jewellery through its website and a growing chain of about 275 stores. Revenue is about INR 17bn. Backed by Accel, Kalaari and Iron Pillar, plus Sunil Kant Munjal, it listed on the NSE and BSE in August 2025. Strong online jewellery brand in India with extensive digital advertising.

Euler Motors is a New Delhi-based Indian electric vehicle maker producing the HiLoad electric three-wheeler cargo vehicle and the Storm electric light truck for last-mile delivery, serving fleet customers. It is backed by Blume Ventures, Lightspeed and Bajaj Auto-linked investors, and has raised about $300m. Private. Strong in the commercial EV segment, with low consumer awareness.

Greenway is an electric vehicle charging network operator based in Bratislava, Slovakia, which runs fast and ultra-fast public chargers across Central and Eastern Europe, including Slovakia, Poland, Czechia and the Balkans. Customers are EV drivers using its app and card, and fleets. Funding is about EUR 273m including investment from Meridiam-style infrastructure investors. Private. Known to EV drivers in the region, little awareness elsewhere.

Motorway is a London-based online used-car selling platform, launched in 2017, where private sellers upload a car and a network of dealers bid, with the seller paying no fee. Dealers pay a fee on completed sales, and it sold over 100,000 cars a year. Backed by DST Global, Highland Europe and others, with funding of about $324m. Private. Well-advertised consumer brand in the UK.

RideNow Powersports is a Chandler, Arizona operator of motorcycle, ATV and powersports dealerships, with over 100 stores in the US selling brands such as Harley-Davidson, Honda, Yamaha, Polaris and Can-Am. It earns from vehicle sales, parts, service and financing. Owned by private equity (Lee Equity Partners and later Argonaut-style sponsors), with funding of about $255m. Private. Recognised by US riders, and active in racing and rally sponsorships.

SEDEMAC is a Pune-based Indian maker of electronic controllers and drives for engines, generators, electric vehicles and appliances, including gensets, diesel engines, e-bikes and e-scooters. It spun out of IIT Bombay research in 2008 and supplies companies such as Mahindra, Kirloskar, Cummins, Honda and Bajaj. Funding is about $260m from investors including Mahindra-linked and ADB-style capital. Private. B2B technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Simple Energy is a Bengaluru-based Indian electric scooter maker, founded in 2019, selling the Simple One and Dot One scooters with a high range, through its own stores, and building a fast-charging network. Backed by Mathew Kuruvilla-led founders, Qualcomm Ventures-style and other investors, it has raised about $280m, including debt. Private. Growing consumer EV brand with limited national awareness.

Suzuki Motor de Mexico is the Mexican subsidiary of Japan's Suzuki Motor Corporation, based in Cuautitlan Izcalli, distributing and marketing Suzuki cars, SUVs and motorcycles in Mexico through a dealer network, and assembling some in Mexico. Funding shown is MXN 4.9bn, a capital-style figure. Subsidiary of Suzuki (Tokyo: 7269). Strong consumer brand in Mexico, with sponsorships in motorsport and local sports.

Anheuser-Busch InBev is the world's largest brewer, headquartered in Leuven, Belgium, with brands including Budweiser, Corona, Stella Artois, Michelob Ultra, Beck's, Skol, Brahma and Modelo. It sells beer and soft drinks in over 150 countries, with revenue near $60bn and about 150,000 employees. Listed on Euronext Brussels (ABI), with secondary listings in Mexico, South Africa and the NYSE. A massive consumer portfolio and a long-time global sports sponsor, including the FIFA World Cup, F1 Budweiser partnerships and the Olympics.

Cruise was a San Francisco autonomous vehicle company majority-owned by General Motors, operating driverless robotaxi services in San Francisco, Austin, Phoenix and other US cities until 2023. After an October 2023 accident and regulatory fallout, operations were suspended, and in December 2024 GM said it would stop funding Cruise's robotaxi work and fold it into GM. Investors included Honda, SoftBank and Microsoft, with funding near $23bn. Effectively wound down, with no commercial relevance as a sponsor.

Flipkart is a Bengaluru-based Indian e-commerce marketplace, selling electronics, fashion, home goods and groceries, and also operating Myntra, Cleartrip and PhonePe previously, to hundreds of millions of customers. Walmart bought a majority stake in 2018 for about $16bn. Funding shown is about $15bn. Private, with a planned IPO. Among India's best-known consumer brands, with heavy advertising and its Big Billion Days sale, plus cricket sponsorship.

Meta Platforms is a Menlo Park, California social technology company that owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads, plus Reality Labs (Quest headsets, Ray-Ban Meta glasses) and Meta AI/Llama models. It serves over three billion daily users and earns mostly from advertising, with revenue above $160bn. Listed on Nasdaq (META). One of the most recognised tech brands globally, a huge advertiser, and an active partner in sports through Ray-Ban Meta and Meta AI deals. Funding shown reflects debt financing.

Project Sopaipilla Holdings is described in Crunchbase as a joint venture involving Meta Platforms, likely a financing vehicle for a large AI data center campus, with about $12.5bn of funding in July 2026. It is a project-finance holding, not an operating consumer business, and the input provides no HQ. Likely B2B infrastructure funding with no consumer brand. Limited detail beyond the input.

Tencent is a Shenzhen-based Chinese technology and entertainment conglomerate, owner of WeChat (over 1.3 billion users), QQ, Tencent Games (Honor of Kings, PUBG Mobile, Riot Games, Supercell), Tencent Cloud, WeChat Pay, Tencent Music and Tencent Video. Revenue is above RMB 600bn. Listed in Hong Kong (0700). Among the world's biggest tech groups, with enormous domestic consumer awareness and sports and esports ties such as NBA digital rights and League of Legends.

Ameren is a St. Louis, Missouri electric and natural gas utility holding company, serving about 2.4 million electric and 900,000 gas customers in Missouri and Illinois via Ameren Missouri, Ameren Illinois and transmission. It earns regulated rates, and revenue is near $7.5bn. Listed on the NYSE (AEE). Utility with strong regional brand recognition and community and sports sponsorship, such as the Cardinals' Ameren-branded partnerships in St. Louis.

AppLovin is a Palo Alto software company whose AXON AI advertising engine matches mobile app and e-commerce advertisers with ad inventory, with a legacy portfolio of mobile games now sold to Tripledot. It earns ad network fees from advertisers and publishers, and revenue has grown to around $5bn with high margins. Listed on Nasdaq (APP) and in the S&P 500. B2B ad-tech with little consumer awareness, though well known with investors.

COFCO Fortune is the food brand and edible oil business of China's state-owned COFCO Group, operating from Beijing and selling Fortune-branded cooking oil, rice, flour, noodles and other packaged foods to Chinese households. Funding of about CNY 21bn came in a 2023 round. State-linked. A major packaged-food consumer brand in China, with extensive retail presence and advertising, little known abroad.

DSV is a Danish global transport and logistics company, headquartered in Hedehusene, near Copenhagen, offering air and sea freight, road transport and contract logistics in about 80 countries. After buying DB Schenker in 2025 for about DKK 106bn, it has more than 150,000 employees, with revenue above DKK 200bn. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (DSV). B2B logistics firm with strong industry reputation, and its trucks and containers carry the brand, but consumers rarely know it.

Heathrow Airport Holdings owns and operates London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport and one of the world's largest hubs, handling about 83 million passengers a year across four terminals. It earns aeronautical charges from airlines and retail, parking and property revenue. Owned by a consortium led by Ferrovial, Qatar Investment Authority, Canada's CDPQ and GIC, Alinda, USS and others, with Ferrovial reducing its stake. Private. Hugely recognised consumer-facing brand, with premium sponsorship opportunities.

J&T Express is an Indonesian-born express delivery company, headquartered in Jakarta, operating a franchised parcel network across Southeast Asia, China, Brazil, Mexico, the Middle East and Africa, handling billions of parcels a year for e-commerce sellers and consumers. It listed in Hong Kong (1519) in 2023. Backed by Sequoia, Hillhouse, Boyu, Tencent and Alibaba-linked investors. A familiar e-commerce logistics brand across Southeast Asia, with football and other sponsorships.

Liquid Intelligent Technologies is a pan-African technology group, with its registered office in Mauritius, and operations run by Strive Masiyiwa's Econet. It provides fibre networks, cloud, cybersecurity, data center and connectivity services to enterprises, governments and telecoms across Africa through brands such as Liquid Cloud and Africa Data Centres, with Cassava Technologies as parent. Private, with funding from development banks. B2B, known to African enterprises and little to consumers.

Main Street Capital is a Houston, Texas business development company providing debt and equity capital to lower-middle-market and middle-market companies in the US, earning interest and dividends and paying monthly dividends to shareholders. It is internally managed, with a portfolio worth about $5bn. Listed on the NYSE (MAIN). B2B-focused investment firm with little consumer awareness.

Masan Group is a Vietnamese consumer and retail conglomerate based in Ho Chi Minh City, owning WinCommerce (WinMart supermarkets), Masan Consumer (Chin-su, Omachi, Nam Ngu sauces), Masan MEATLife and a stake in Techcombank. It sells to Vietnamese households and has revenue near VND 80 trillion. Listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (MSN). Strong, widely advertised consumer brands in Vietnam, and a sports sponsor.

MKS Instruments is an Andover, Massachusetts supplier of instruments, subsystems and process control solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, electronics, advanced materials and life sciences, including vacuum, laser, photonics and power products, many from its 2016 acquisition of Newport and 2022 Atotech deal. Revenue is near $3.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MKSI). B2B industrial technology brand, with no consumer awareness.

Mobileye is an Israeli driver-assistance and autonomous driving technology company, headquartered in Jerusalem, whose EyeQ chips and vision software are fitted in tens of millions of cars from automakers such as Volkswagen, Ford, BMW and Nissan. It also develops robotaxi and self-driving systems. Intel acquired it in 2017 and relisted it on Nasdaq (MBLY) in 2022, retaining majority ownership. B2B technology supplier, with strong awareness in automotive circles and little among consumers.

Philips (Koninklijke Philips) is a Dutch health technology company based in Amsterdam, selling medical imaging, patient monitoring, sleep and respiratory devices, and personal health products such as Sonicare toothbrushes and Avent baby products. Revenue is about EUR 18bn with around 70,000 employees. It sold off its lighting arm (Signify) and TV business. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam and NYSE (PHG). A long-standing household brand with global recognition, and sports sponsorship history, including football's PSV Eindhoven.

Shein is a Singapore-headquartered online fast-fashion retailer, founded in China by Chris Xu, selling inexpensive apparel, beauty, home goods and accessories directly to consumers in over 150 countries via its app and website, using a quick on-demand supply chain. Revenue is estimated near $30-40bn. Valued at about $66bn in 2023 and pursuing a London or Hong Kong listing. Private. Extremely high consumer awareness among younger shoppers, with active influencer marketing, though under scrutiny for labour and environmental practices.

Valentino is a Milan-based Italian luxury fashion house, founded in 1960 in Rome by Valentino Garavani and Giancarlo Giammetti, selling ready-to-wear, accessories, shoes, beauty and fragrance through boutiques, department stores and e-commerce worldwide, with revenue near EUR 1.4bn. Qatar's Mayhoola owns it, and Kering agreed in 2023 to buy a 30 percent stake, rising to full ownership by 2028. Private. Globally recognised luxury brand, with the red Valentino colour as an asset; limited sports ties.

Vietnam Airlines is Vietnam's state-owned flag carrier, based in Hanoi, with a fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft (including A350 and 787) flying to over 20 countries and many domestic routes under the Golden Lotus brand, and a member of SkyTeam. It carries over 20 million passengers a year, with Vietnam Airlines Group also owning Pacific Airlines and VASCO. Majority-owned by the government through SCIC and listed on the Vietnamese UPCoM market (HVN). Strongly recognised by Vietnamese consumers, with sports and event sponsorships.

Yinwang Smart Technology (Yinwang Intelligent Technology, Shenzhen Yinwang) is Huawei's intelligent automotive solutions business, created in 2023 as a Huawei subsidiary to supply ADS driver assistance, HarmonyOS cockpits and electric drive systems to Chinese carmakers for HIMA vehicles such as Aito, Luxeed, Stelato and Maextro. Changan Automobile bought a 10 percent stake in 2024 for CNY 11.5bn. Private. A technology supplier, with strong consumer awareness because of the Huawei brand in China.

Dayforce (formerly Ceridian) is a Minneapolis-based cloud human capital management software company, supplying payroll, HR, time and attendance, benefits and talent tools to mid-market and large employers in North America and abroad. Revenue is above $1.8bn. Thoma Bravo agreed to take it private in 2025 in an $12.3bn deal, after which it left the NYSE (DAY). B2B software with solid HR industry recognition, and little consumer awareness.

America Movil is a Mexico City-based mobile and fixed telecom giant controlled by Carlos Slim's family, with about 300 million wireless subscribers in Mexico (Telcel), Brazil (Claro), Colombia, Argentina, Chile, Central America and parts of Europe (A1, Telekom Austria). Revenue is about $50bn. Listed on the Mexican exchange (AMX) and NYSE. Very strong consumer brands Telcel and Claro across Latin America, with major sports sponsorships, notably in football and motorsport, including Telmex-Telcel's long F1 history with Sergio Perez.

Applied Materials is a Santa Clara, California supplier of semiconductor and display manufacturing equipment, including deposition, etch, ion implant and inspection tools, plus services, serving chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung and Intel. Revenue is near $28bn with about 35,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (AMAT). B2B equipment maker, one of the world's largest in its field, with little consumer awareness.

Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL) operates Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, India's third busiest airport, handling over 40 million passengers a year, with a new Terminal 2. It earns airline charges, retail, advertising and property income. Owned by the GVK Group's successor Fairfax, Fairfax India Holdings (about 64 percent), with Siemens-related and Karnataka government stakes. Private. Consumer-facing airport brand in a major city, with sponsorship and advertising inventory.

Bridge Data Centres is a Singapore-based hyperscale data center developer and operator in Asia-Pacific, with campuses in Malaysia, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, India, Thailand, Australia and Japan, serving cloud, internet and enterprise customers. Founded in 2019, it was acquired by Bain Capital and is a standalone brand. Private, with funding of about $2.8bn. B2B infrastructure with no consumer awareness.

Caris Life Sciences is an Irving, Texas AI-enabled precision medicine company providing molecular profiling of tumours, with whole exome and transcriptome sequencing, to guide cancer treatment choices for oncologists and biopharma partners. It generated revenue above $400m before its June 2025 IPO on Nasdaq (CAI). Founded by David Halbert. Customers are hospitals, doctors and drug developers. Mostly B2B and clinician-facing, with modest direct consumer awareness.

Celonis is a Munich and New York process mining and execution management software company, helping large organisations analyse how business processes run and fix inefficiencies using its Process Intelligence platform. Customers include Siemens, Uber, Coca-Cola and other large enterprises. It was valued at $13bn in 2022, with total funding around $2.4bn from Accel, 83North and Arena Holdings. Private.
