B2B software well known to IT leaders and consultants, with little consumer awareness, though it is a known sports sponsor.

Check Point Software Technologies is a cybersecurity company founded in Israel, with US headquarters in Redwood City and its main office in Tel Aviv, selling network firewalls, cloud security, endpoint, email and threat prevention products (Quantum, Harmony, CloudGuard) to over 100,000 organisations. Revenue is about $2.6bn. Listed on Nasdaq (CHKP). B2B brand with strong IT security recognition, and sponsorship activity including a long-running Formula 1 relationship with Scuderia Ferrari-related partners in the past.

Checkout.com is a London-based global payments company, founded in 2012, which provides card acquiring, payment processing, fraud tools and payouts to merchants like Netflix, eBay, Shein, Sony and Samsung. It handles over $300bn in processed volume and was valued at $40bn in 2022, then marked down to $12bn in 2025. Private. B2B fintech, well known in e-commerce and payments, with its brand showing in sports sponsorship, such as Formula 1 and the Premier League.

Clio is a Burnaby, British Columbia cloud legal practice management software company, serving law firms with case management, billing, client intake and AI tools (Clio Manage, Clio Grow, Clio Work), with over 150,000 users. It raised $900m in 2025 at a $5bn valuation and agreed to buy vLex for about $1bn. Founded in 2008. Private. B2B software with strong awareness among lawyers and little in the general public.

Diebold Nixdorf is a North Canton, Ohio supplier of ATMs, self-checkout, point-of-sale systems and related software and services to banks and retailers worldwide, with roughly 20,000 employees and revenue near $3.7bn. It restructured through a Chapter 11 filing in 2023 and emerged with debt reduced, relisting on the NYSE (DBD). B2B equipment brand, the ATMs are widely seen though consumers seldom know the brand.

gategroup is a Swiss airline catering and onboard services company, based in Glattbrugg near Zurich, supplying meals, retail products, equipment and lounges to airlines worldwide through more than 190 units in about 60 countries. It was acquired by RRJ Capital in 2016 and later had HNA and Temasek links, restructured and sold to new owners. Private. B2B with little consumer brand recognition, though its products are used on airlines passengers' flights.

General Mills is a Minneapolis-based global packaged food company with brands such as Cheerios, Nature Valley, Haagen-Dazs, Pillsbury, Betty Crocker, Yoplait, Old El Paso, Blue Buffalo pet food and Annie's. It sells through grocery and foodservice channels in more than 100 countries, with revenue near $19bn and about 34,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (GIS). Highly recognised consumer brands in North America and abroad, with large advertising budgets and sports sponsorships.

Gigaclear is a UK full-fibre broadband provider based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, building gigabit networks in rural villages and small towns and selling broadband to homes and businesses, and wholesale. Revenue is under GBP 100m, with debt financing and equity from investors including Infracapital (M&G) and Universities Superannuation Scheme. Private. Regional consumer broadband brand, with limited national awareness.

Gol Linhas Aereas (Gol Transportes Aereos) is a Brazilian low-cost airline based in Sao Paulo, flying a Boeing 737 fleet on domestic and South American routes, with more than 30 million passengers a year. It filed for US Chapter 11 in January 2024 and emerged in June 2025 with Abra Group as its parent, after which it delisted from the NYSE and B3. Revenue is near BRL 20bn. Well-known Brazilian consumer airline brand, with football and sports sponsorship history.

Great Rock Capital is a Westport, Connecticut asset-based lender providing senior secured loans to middle-market companies, including retail, consumer and industrial firms, backed by inventory, receivables and equipment. It earns interest and fees, and is owned by Great Rock Capital Partners Management with institutional investors. Private. B2B specialist finance firm with no consumer awareness.

KnowBe4 is a Clearwater, Florida security awareness training and simulated phishing platform used by over 70,000 organisations to train employees. Vista Equity Partners took it private in 2023 for about $4.6bn, and it later acquired Egress and was folded into the KnowBe4 and Egress offering. Revenue was near $350m before the buyout. Private. B2B cybersecurity brand with high awareness among IT teams but little consumer awareness.

Legrand is a French maker of electrical and digital building infrastructure, based near Limoges and managed from Croissy-Beaubourg, producing switches, sockets, cable management, data center power and connected home products under brands such as Legrand, Bticino and Arnould. Revenue is about EUR 8.5bn with over 38,000 employees, selling in nearly 90 countries. Listed on Euronext Paris (LR). B2B and installer-focused, but switches and sockets are in most European homes; modest consumer brand awareness.

Lowell Group is a UK-based credit management company, from Leeds, which buys and collects consumer debt, owning brands such as Lowell, Fredrikson & Associates and Carrington Law, with operations in the UK, Germany, the Nordics and the Netherlands. It serves banks, utilities and telecoms, earning recoveries. Owned by Permira and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan after a 2017-18 buyout. Private. B2B debt purchaser with low consumer brand goodwill.

LPL Financial is the largest independent broker-dealer in the US, headquartered in San Diego, Boston and Fort Mill, supporting more than 22,000 financial advisors with brokerage, advisory, custody, research and technology platforms, and about $1.7 trillion in client assets. Revenue is above $10bn. Listed on Nasdaq (LPLA). Advisor-facing brand, advertised to retail investors through its Independent firms, with moderate awareness.

Majid Al Futtaim is a Dubai-based Emirati conglomerate, founded in 1992 by Majid Al Futtaim, that owns and operates the Mall of the Emirates, City Centre malls, Carrefour franchise stores in the Middle East, Africa and Asia, VOX Cinemas, Ski Dubai and Magic Planet, plus retail brands and a consumer finance unit. It employs over 40,000 people, with revenue of roughly $10bn. Privately held by the Majid Al Futtaim family. Very high consumer visibility in the Gulf.

MSCI is a New York provider of investment indexes, analytics, ESG ratings and risk models, including the MSCI World and Emerging Markets indexes, used by asset managers, banks and pension funds worldwide. It earns subscriptions and asset-based fees from index-linked products, with revenue near $3bn. Listed on the NYSE (MSCI). B2B financial data company with strong finance-industry recognition and no general consumer awareness.

OSI Systems is a Hawthorne, California designer and maker of security screening systems (Rapiscan), healthcare patient monitoring (Spacelabs) and optoelectronic devices, with products sold to airports, customs agencies, hospitals and electronics firms in over 100 countries. Revenue is near $1.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (OSIS). B2B and government supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Progress Software is a Burlington, Massachusetts enterprise software company selling application development, data integration, content management and cybersecurity tools, such as Telerik, Sitefinity, MarkLogic, MOVEit and ShareFile, to developers and businesses. Revenue is around $950m. Listed on Nasdaq (PRGS). B2B software with recognition among developers, and little consumer awareness.

Quantum Computing Inc. is a Hoboken, New Jersey company, listed on Nasdaq (QUBT), developing photonic quantum technologies such as thin-film lithium niobate chips and quantum optics for sensing, computing and security. It has raised capital through private placements, giving it a cash pile near $1.5bn. Revenue is tiny. Speculative technology company with a strong retail-investor following but no consumer products.

RingCentral is a Belmont, California cloud communications company providing business phone, video meetings (RingEX), contact centre and AI tools, for companies of all sizes, with revenue near $2.4bn. Customers range from small businesses to large enterprises, paying subscription fees. Listed on the NYSE (RNG). B2B brand with strong awareness among IT buyers, plus sports sponsorship including the Rocket Mortgage-style naming deals and NASCAR in the past.

Rippling is a San Francisco workforce management platform combining HR, payroll, IT device management, spend and benefits in one system, serving tens of thousands of businesses, from start-ups to mid-size firms. Founded in 2016 by Parker Conrad, it raised $450m in 2025 at a $16.8bn valuation, led by Elad Gil and Baillie Gifford. Private. B2B software with high recognition among HR and start-up leaders, and an active marketing and sponsorship presence in sports, including with F1 teams.

S&P Global is a New York financial data and analytics group, owning S&P Global Ratings, S&P Global Market Intelligence, S&P Dow Jones Indices (the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average), Platts and Mobility (including CARFAX), and reporting revenue near $14bn. Customers are investors, banks, corporates and governments. Listed on the NYSE (SPGI). Strong B2B brand, with the S&P 500 known to the public, and sponsors in finance and sport.

The GEO Group is a Boca Raton, Florida operator of private prisons, immigration detention centres, rehabilitation programmes and electronic monitoring services under contract to governments in the US, plus Australia and South Africa. Its largest customers are US federal agencies, such as ICE, and revenue is about $2.4bn. Listed on the NYSE (GEO). Controversial government contractor, low consumer visibility and significant reputational sensitivity for sponsorship.

TierPoint is a St. Louis-based US data center and cloud services provider offering colocation, managed hosting, disaster recovery and cybersecurity from about 30 data centers, serving mid-market enterprises. It is backed by Brightstar and Wafra, with large debt facilities (raised $2.4bn including financing), and acquired several smaller operators. Private. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Viacom18 Digital Ventures (JioCinema's holding entity) was the Indian streaming and digital media company, based in Mumbai, a joint venture between Reliance Industries' Viacom18 and Bodhi Tree Systems (James Murdoch and Uday Shankar), which ran JioCinema, streaming IPL and other sports rights. It merged with Disney Star in 2024 to form JioStar, creating Jio Hotstar. Funding of INR 204bn reflects Bodhi Tree's investment. Now part of JioStar, one of India's biggest media brands.

Vinted is a Lithuanian online marketplace for second-hand fashion, based in Vilnius, where individuals buy and sell clothes, shoes and accessories, with buyers paying a protection fee. It has over 100 million registered members in about 20 markets across Europe and the US, and reported revenue of around EUR 800m. Valued at EUR 5bn in a 2024 secondary sale. Private, backed by Insight and Accel. Strong consumer brand across Europe, with large advertising spending.

Virgin Atlantic Airways is a British long-haul airline based in Crawley, West Sussex, flying from London Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester to North America, the Caribbean, Africa, India and Asia, with about 40 aircraft and over 5 million passengers a year. Delta Air Lines holds 49 percent, Virgin Group 51 percent, and the airline is private. It emerged from a 2020 rescue package. Strong consumer brand with the Virgin name, and sponsorship and brand tie-ins.

Waystar is a Louisville, Kentucky healthcare payments software company providing cloud-based revenue cycle tools, claims, patient payments and prior authorisation services to hospitals, health systems and physician groups. Revenue is around $1bn. Listed on Nasdaq (WAY) since its 2024 IPO, controlled by EQT and CPP Investments. B2B software, known to healthcare finance teams, with no consumer awareness.

WeRide is an autonomous driving company founded in China and now with a San Jose and Guangzhou presence, developing robotaxis, robobuses, robovans and driver assistance, with operations in China, the UAE, Singapore and Europe, with partners such as Uber, Nissan and Renault. It listed on Nasdaq (WRD) in 2024 and later added a Hong Kong listing. Funding is about $1.8bn. B2B and fleet-oriented, with growing visibility in the UAE and Chinese cities.

Avril Group is a Paris-based French agro-industrial and financial group, created by French farmers' organisations, owning edible oil and biofuel producer Saipol, Lesieur and Puget (consumer oil brands), Sofiproteol, Diester and animal nutrition business Sanders. Revenue is near EUR 9-10bn. It is a cooperative-style group, not listed. Several household food brands in France, with the Lesieur oil brand widely recognised, otherwise B2B.

Big Brand Tire and Service is a Moorpark, California tire and auto service retailer, with dozens of stores in California and the Western US, selling tires, wheels, brakes and repairs to consumers and fleets. It is private, owned by PE-backed Mavis-style consolidators. The input shows funding of about $1.6bn, which probably reflects a transaction or debt. Local consumer brand with moderate regional recognition.

BigBasket is a Bengaluru-based Indian online grocery and supermarket business offering scheduled and quick delivery of fruit, vegetables, groceries and household goods in more than 25 Indian cities. Tata Digital bought a majority stake in 2021 and it is part of the Tata Group, with Alibaba and Abraaj as earlier investors. Revenue is around INR 100bn. Private. Strong urban consumer brand in India with substantial advertising.

Cenomi Retail (formerly Fawaz Alhokair Group) is a Riyadh-based Saudi lifestyle retailer, operating and franchising international fashion, footwear, food and beauty brands such as Zara, H&M, Marks and Spencer, Mothercare and Bath and Body Works in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and across the Middle East. It is linked to Cenomi Centers, the mall owner, and Cenomi Group. Listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul: 4240). Household name for Saudi shoppers, with many consumer-facing stores.

Clikalia is a Madrid-based Spanish proptech company that buys flats directly from owners, renovates them and sells them on, with an online process for quick offers, operating in Spain, Portugal and Italy. It makes money on property resale and financing, and has raised about EUR 1.1bn, including debt. Private. Consumer property brand with modest awareness in Spain, and some sports sponsorship.

Coca-Cola Consolidated is a Charlotte, North Carolina bottler and distributor, the largest independent Coca-Cola bottler in the US, producing and distributing Coca-Cola products, plus other brands, in about 14 states across the southeast, mid-Atlantic and Midwest. Revenue is near $7bn. Controlled by chairman J. Frank Harrison III, and listed on Nasdaq (COKE). B2B2C distributor with local branding, and the Coca-Cola logo on products; the bottler name itself is not a consumer brand.

Domino's Pizza is an Ann Arbor, Michigan pizza chain with over 21,000 stores in more than 90 countries, mostly franchised, including delivery and carry-out, with strong digital ordering. System-wide sales are above $19bn. Master franchisees such as Domino's Pizza Enterprises (Australia) and DP Eurasia operate abroad. Listed on the NYSE (DPZ). Very high consumer brand awareness, with big advertising spend and sports sponsorships, such as NASCAR and MLS.

Entain is a London-based global sports betting and gaming group, with brands including Ladbrokes, Coral, bwin, Sportingbet, Eurobet, PartyCasino and a 50 percent stake in BetMGM in the US, plus Gala Bingo and TAB in Australia. It operates in many regulated markets, with revenue near GBP 5bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (ENT), formerly GVC Holdings. Strong consumer brands, with a heavy football and sports marketing record; regulation limits motorsport tie-ups in some markets.

Groupon is a Chicago online marketplace offering discounted deals on local services, travel, restaurants and goods to consumers, funded by merchants' commissions. Founded in 2008, it once had a $13bn market value but has since shrunk, with revenue under $500m, and shifted to a focus on local experiences. Listed on Nasdaq (GRPN). Widely recognised consumer brand from its early deal-of-the-day era, now much smaller.

Haldiram's Snacks is the Noida, Uttar Pradesh-based Indian snack food company behind Haldiram's bhujia, namkeen, sweets, ready-to-eat meals and packaged foods, sold through retail in India and exported to dozens of countries. It is a family-founded group with Bikaner, Nagpur and Delhi entities. In 2025 Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Alpha Wave and Temasek bought minority stakes valuing it at around $10bn. Private. Beloved Indian consumer brand with big advertising reach.

J.B. Poindexter and Co. is a Houston, Texas privately held diversified manufacturer, owning businesses that produce truck bodies (Morgan Truck Body, Morgan Olson), pickup truck accessories (Truck Accessories Group, including Leer), specialty vehicles, and EFP/Reading Truck Body-style components. Customers are fleet operators, delivery firms and consumers. Controlled by chairman John Poindexter, with revenue around $1.5bn. Private. B2B brand known in fleet and truck circles, not to the public.

Melco Resorts and Entertainment is a Hong Kong-based casino resort developer and operator with properties in Macau (City of Dreams, Studio City, Altira), Manila (City of Dreams Manila) and Cyprus. Led by Lawrence Ho, it earns from gaming, rooms, dining, entertainment and retail, with revenue near US$4.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MLCO) and Hong Kong (6883). Strong consumer brand in Asian gaming and tourism, and a notable sponsor with a Macau Grand Prix link.

Mohegan Gaming and Entertainment is a Uncasville, Connecticut casino operator owned by the Mohegan Tribe of Indians of Connecticut, running Mohegan Sun, Mohegan Pennsylvania, Resorts Casino in Atlantic City and other gaming venues in the US, Canada and abroad, and the Inspire resort near Seoul. Revenue is above $1.6bn from gaming, hotels and entertainment. Tribal-owned. Strong regional consumer brand, with sports sponsorship, such as WNBA's Connecticut Sun, which it formerly owned.

Premium Brands Holdings is a Richmond, British Columbia food manufacturer and distributor, producing specialty foods such as sandwiches, deli meats, Italian meats, protein and snacks, and distributing wholesale food products across Canada and the western US. Revenue is around C$6.5bn. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (PBH). Largely B2B (grocery and foodservice supply), with some private-label work, so consumer brand awareness is low.

Ralph Lauren is a New York luxury and lifestyle fashion company selling apparel, footwear, accessories, fragrance and home goods under Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Polo Ralph Lauren, Lauren and Double RL. It sells through wholesale, its own stores and e-commerce globally, with revenue near $7bn. Founder Ralph Lauren holds control. Listed on the NYSE (RL). Iconic consumer fashion brand, a long-time sports partner (US Open, Wimbledon, The Masters, Team USA), and visible across the sports and luxury market.

SharkNinja is a Needham, Massachusetts maker of household appliances, with the Shark brand of vacuums, steam cleaners and air purifiers and the Ninja brand of blenders, air fryers, coffee makers and grills, plus Beast and Shark Beauty products. It sells through retail and online in North America, Europe and Asia, with revenue near $6bn. Listed on the NYSE (SN) since 2023 after separating from JS Global. Very strong consumer brands and heavy advertising; Shark has sponsored sports, notably NASCAR and others.

Tripadvisor is a Needham, Massachusetts travel platform where users read reviews and book hotels, tours, restaurants (via TheFork) and experiences, with brands including Viator, TheFork and Tripadvisor itself. It earns commissions and advertising and has revenue of about $1.8bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TRIP), with Liberty TripAdvisor merged in 2025. Very high consumer awareness in travel, with a community of reviewers and advertising partnerships.

Vantage Studios is a subsidiary of Ubisoft, formed in 2025 with Tencent investing EUR 1.16bn for a 25 percent stake, based in Montreuil near Paris, to operate the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Rainbow Six franchises. It sells games to consumers through digital and retail and earns subscription and live-service revenue. Controlled by Ubisoft (Euronext: UBI) with Tencent as a minority holder. Strong consumer franchise brands, though Vantage as a corporate name is new.

Vuori is a Carlsbad, California premium activewear and athleisure brand, founded in 2015, selling performance joggers, shorts, tops and outerwear for men and women through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale partners. Revenue is estimated near $1bn+, and it was valued at $5.5bn in a 2024 round led by Norwest and others, with additional investors. Private. Fast-growing lifestyle brand with strong social media following, particularly among men in the US.

Accel Entertainment is a Bolingbrook, Illinois distributed gaming operator, placing video gaming terminals and sweepstakes machines in bars, restaurants and gaming cafes in Illinois, Nevada, Montana, Pennsylvania and other states, sharing revenue with venue owners. Revenue is about $1.2bn. Listed on the NYSE (ACEL). B2B route operator whose brand is little known to consumers.

Ashford Hospitality Trust is a Dallas, Texas hotel REIT that owns upscale and upper-midscale hotels across the US, mainly under Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt brands, advised by Ashford Inc. It earns revenue from hotel operations and has been highly leveraged, with a shrinking portfolio. Listed on the NYSE (AHT). Property owner, guests see the franchise brand rather than Ashford, so consumer awareness is low.

Boots UK is a Nottingham-based British pharmacy and health and beauty retailer, with about 2,000 stores, selling prescriptions, medicines, cosmetics, toiletries and own-label products such as No7, Soap and Glory and Boots Own Brand, plus the Advantage Card loyalty scheme. It is owned by Walgreens Boots Alliance, which was taken private by Sycamore Partners in 2025. Private. Very strong UK high street consumer brand, with a history of sports partnerships.

Del Monte Foods is a Walnut Creek, California US maker of canned fruit, vegetables and tomatoes under Del Monte, Contadina, S&W and College Inn, sold in supermarkets nationwide, with ownership by Del Monte Pacific (Philippines). It filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025 and sold most assets to buyers, including Fresh Del Monte-style and private-equity buyers. Funding shown is about $912m, reflecting financing. Well-known US grocery brand, though now restructured and parted out.

Dine Brands Global is a Pasadena, California restaurant franchisor, owning Applebee's Neighborhood Grill + Bar, IHOP and Fuzzy's Taco Shop, with about 3,500 restaurants in the US and abroad, nearly all franchised. It earns royalties and franchise fees, with revenue near $0.9bn. Listed on the NYSE (DIN). Applebee's and IHOP are very recognisable casual dining brands in the US, with strong advertising and sports and entertainment tie-ins.

Fosun Tourism Group is a Shanghai-based Chinese resort and travel group owned by Fosun International, operating Club Med (acquired 2015), Atlantis Sanya, Thomas Cook brand assets in some markets and Foliday and Lijiang resorts. It earns room, tour and resort revenue. It listed in Hong Kong in 2018 (1992) and was later delisted from the Hong Kong market after Fosun's takeover. Club Med is a notable global leisure brand, popular in Europe and Asia.

Klook is a Singapore-based travel and leisure booking platform where users book attractions, tours, transport and activities, with a focus on Asia-Pacific travellers and destinations worldwide. It operates in over 2,500 destinations, with tens of millions of users and revenue of several hundred million dollars. Funding of about $1bn includes SoftBank, Sequoia, and Goldman Sachs. Private, preparing an IPO. Strong awareness among travellers in Asia, with partnerships in sports and travel.

Light and Wonder is a Las Vegas gaming technology company that makes slot machines, casino management systems, table games and iGaming content, plus the SciPlay social casino unit that it has since sold. It supplies casinos and online operators globally, earning product sales and gaming revenue shares, with revenue near $3.2bn. Formerly Scientific Games, it listed on Nasdaq (LNW). B2B brand known in casinos, not by consumers.

Oddity Tech is a New York and Tel Aviv-based consumer tech company that builds digital-first beauty and wellness brands, including Il Makiage and SpoiledChild, using data-driven direct-to-consumer marketing. Its customers are mainly women shopping online, and it earns product sales with revenue near $800m. Listed on Nasdaq (ODD) since 2023. Il Makiage is a very heavily advertised online beauty brand, particularly on social media.

Quirch Foods is a Coral Gables, Florida food distributor and exporter of beef, pork, poultry and seafood, supplying supermarkets, foodservice and processors across Latin America, the Caribbean and the US from US and international suppliers. It was created by Quirch family and was combined with Sysco-related businesses. Privately held. B2B protein supplier with little consumer awareness.

Scentre Group is a Sydney-based owner and operator of Westfield shopping centres in Australia and New Zealand, including Westfield Sydney, Bondi Junction and Chermside, with about 40 centres hosting thousands of retailers. It earns rent and fees, and manages around A$50bn of assets. Listed on the ASX (SCG), spun out of Westfield Group in 2014. Westfield is a very recognisable Australian mall brand, with significant advertising and event sponsorship inventory.

Skims is a Culver City, California shapewear, loungewear and underwear brand co-founded by Kim Kardashian and Emma Grede in 2019, selling directly to consumers online, via its own stores and select retailers like Nordstrom. Revenue is estimated near $1bn. It raised $225m in 2025 at a $5bn valuation, with Wellington, Imaginary Ventures and others. Private. Extremely visible consumer fashion brand, driven by celebrity and social media, and official underwear partner of Team USA.

Vail Resorts is a Broomfield, Colorado operator of about 40 mountain resorts, including Vail, Whistler Blackcomb, Park City, Breckenridge, Heavenly and Perisher, plus lodging and retail. It earns lift ticket, Epic Pass, ski school and dining revenue from skiers across North America, Europe and Australia, with revenue near $2.9bn. Listed on the NYSE (MTN). Strong brand among snow sports enthusiasts, and a notable sports and events promoter.

Welcome Break is a UK motorway service area operator, based in Newport Pagnell, Buckinghamshire, running about 40 sites with fuel stations, Starbucks, KFC, Burger King, M&S Food and Greggs outlets, plus Days Inn hotels. Roughly 50 million visitors a year pass through. Owned by the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, after Starwood's earlier ownership. Private. Familiar to UK drivers, with a retail-led brand, and potential for hospitality tie-ins.

Calidda is Gas Natural de Lima y Callao, the Lima-based Peruvian company that distributes natural gas to homes, businesses, industry and vehicles in Lima and Callao, with a concession covering millions of residents. It earns regulated tariffs for gas connections and supply. Owned mostly by Grupo Energia Bogota (Colombia), with Promigas. Private. Utility brand well known in Lima, with some community sponsorship, and an automotive gas conversion business.

Moove is a Lagos, Nigeria-based mobility fintech that finances vehicles for ride-hailing and delivery drivers, offering vehicle leases, fleet management and revenue-based financing across Africa, India and the UK, working with Uber, Bolt and Lyft partners. It raised about $694m, including a $100m Series B from Uber and Mubadala in 2023. Private. Known among rideshare drivers and fleet operators, with limited public consumer awareness.

DANA (Dompet Digital Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based Indonesian digital wallet and payments app, used for QR payments, bill payments, transfers and e-commerce, with tens of millions of users. It is backed by Emtek Group and Ant Group, with a funding figure of about $554m. Private. Strong consumer fintech brand in Indonesia, with heavy promotion and sponsorship in local sports and events.

DeepWay is a Hefei, Anhui-based Chinese company developing intelligent electric heavy-duty trucks and autonomous driving systems for logistics, including electric and hydrogen trucks, as part of Baidu's former and Chinese investor-backed commercial vehicle push. It has raised about $590m, with a January 2026 round. Private, with an IPO plan in Hong Kong. B2B logistics technology brand, known in Chinese trucking, with no consumer awareness.
